children.title: Online Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Sequential irrevocable packing.

assumptions_latex: Items arrive sequentially with sizes \(0<s_t\leq1\).
A placed item cannot subsequently be moved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An online algorithm must choose each feasible bin using only the revealed prefix; performance is measured against the offline optimum on the completed sequence.

notation.meaning: bins used by online algorithm A

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical irrevocable one-dimensional online bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In online bin packing, items \(s_1,\ldots,s_n\in(0,1]\) are revealed one at a time. Upon receiving \(s_t\), an algorithm must irrevocably assign it to an already opened bin whose current load plus \(s_t\) is at most \(1\), or open a new bin; its decision may depend only on \((s_1,\ldots,s_t)\). For a deterministic algorithm \(A\), its asymptotic competitive ratio is \[R_A=\limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \sup_{\sigma:\operatorname{OPT}(\sigma)\geq N}\frac{A(\sigma)}{\operatorname{OPT}(\sigma)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Online bin packing places each arriving item irrevocably using only the revealed prefix and compares its bin count with the completed sequence's offline optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Online Bin Packing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition consistently specifies deterministic irrevocable online packing and its asymptotic competitive ratio, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Migration-Recourse Packing Family
children.top_down_role: Sequential packing with controlled migration or reassignment.

children.title: Repacking Models
children.top_down_role: Sequential packing variants permitting reassignment of previously packed items.

assumptions_latex: Items arrive in a finite update sequence, and every item size lies in \((0,1]\).
After each update, all active items must be assigned to identical unit-capacity bins.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible repacking schedule minimizes a prescribed packing objective while respecting the model's migration or recourse restriction at every update.

notation.meaning: active item set after update t
items whose assigned bin changes at update t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic identical-bin model allowing assignments of previously packed items to change after updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_0,I_1,\ldots,I_T\) be active item sets with sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\). A repacking schedule is a sequence \((P_t)_{t=0}^T\) such that each \(P_t\) partitions \(I_t\) into bins \(B\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in B}s_i\le 1\). For \(t\ge 1\), an item in \(I_{t-1}\cap I_t\) is migrated when its bin in \(P_t\) differs from its bin in \(P_{t-1}\); the migrated set is \(M_t\). A repacking model specifies an objective for \(P_t\) and a restriction or charge on \(M_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repacking model maintains feasible bin assignments over updates and permits previously packed items to move, subject to an explicit migration restriction or cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Repacking Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the chosen repacking convention. In particular, migration based on a changed bin requires a persistent or matched bin identity across consecutive packings; otherwise the migrated set is not well-defined.

children.title: Limited-Recourse Models
children.top_down_role: Sequential variants imposing explicit limits on reassignment.

assumptions_latex: A feasible packing exists immediately before and after each update.
Recourse counts only active items whose assigned bin changes across the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule has recourse bound \(r\) precisely when \(|M_t|\le r\) for every update \(t\).

notation.meaning: maximum permitted item moves per update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case item-move recourse for dynamic identical-bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider consecutive feasible packings \(P_{t-1}\) and \(P_t\) of the active items before and after update \(t\). Let \(M_t\) contain every surviving item whose assigned bin changes, counting an item once even if the implementation moves it repeatedly. The packing schedule has per-update item recourse at most \(r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\) if \(|M_t|\le r\) for every \(t\). It has amortized item recourse at most \(r\) if \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}|M_t|\le rT\) for every finite prefix of \(T\) updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limited recourse bounds either the worst-case or amortized number of surviving items reassigned when the packing instance changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Recourse Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent given an established migrated-item set, but no source supports the selected surviving-item, per-update, and prefix-amortized accounting conventions.

children.title: Migration-Budget Regimes
children.top_down_role: Model classes distinguished by the permitted amount or cost of migration.

assumptions_latex: Every item has size \(s_i\in(0,1]\).
Update \(t\) inserts or deletes an item of size \(u_t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A migration-factor budget \(\beta\) requires \(\sum_{i\in M_t}s_i\le\beta u_t\), with analogous cumulative inequalities for amortized budgets.

notation.meaning: size of the item inserted or deleted at update t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size-weighted worst-case and amortized migration budgets for single-item updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For update \(t\), define migrated volume \(V_t=\sum_{i\in M_t}s_i\), where \(M_t\) contains surviving items assigned to different bins after the update. A worst-case migration-factor regime with factor \(\beta\ge 0\) imposes \(V_t\le\beta u_t\) for every \(t\). An amortized regime imposes \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}V_t\le\beta\sum_{t=1}^{T}u_t\) for every finite prefix \(T\). An absolute-volume regime instead fixes \(B\ge0\) and requires either \(V_t\le B\) per update or \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}V_t\le BT\) amortized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Migration budgets may bound moved item volume per update, over update prefixes, relative to update size, or by an absolute allowance.
knowledge_statements.title: Migration-Budget Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the stated worst-case, amortized, relative-volume, and absolute-volume regimes, especially the use of deleted-item size as the update budget denominator.

children.title: Bin-Type Content-Constraint Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Variants changing bin types or admissible bin contents.

children.title: Capacity-Cost Bin Family
children.top_down_role: Multiple available bin capacities or costs.

children.title: Variable-Sized Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Packing with multiple available bin capacities.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Sized Bin Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-type variable-sized packing with type-dependent capacities and opening costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given item sizes \(s_1,\ldots,s_n>0\) and bin types \(k\in K\) with capacity \(C_k>0\) and cost \(c_k\ge0\), variable-sized bin packing chooses nonnegative integers \(y_k\) and assigns every item to one of the resulting bins. Each opened type-\(k\) bin containing item set \(B\) must satisfy \(\sum_{i\in B}s_i\le C_k\). The objective is \(\min\sum_{k\in K}c_ky_k\). Unlimited supply means \(y_k\) is unrestricted; a bounded-supply variant additionally imposes \(y_k\le a_k\) for given availabilities \(a_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Items are packed into chosen bin types with differing capacities and costs, minimizing the total cost of opened bins.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many bin types with positive capacities and nonnegative opening costs.
Every item must be assigned to exactly one opened bin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the minimum total opening cost over all type selections and capacity-feasible assignments.

notation.meaning: capacity and cost of bin type k
number of opened bins of type k

children.title: Costed Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Packing where bin use carries type-dependent costs.

assumptions_latex: Candidate bins have specified capacities, opening costs, and eligibility sets.
Each item must be assigned to one opened eligible bin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum-cost feasible packing minimizes \(\sum_{j\in J}c_jy_j\) subject to assignment and capacity constraints.

notation.meaning: capacity and opening cost of candidate bin j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate-bin formulation with heterogeneous opening costs, capacities, and optional assignment eligibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite item set with sizes \(s_i>0\), and let \(J\) be candidate bins with capacities \(C_j>0\), costs \(c_j\ge0\), and eligible item sets \(E_j\subseteq I\). Costed bin packing chooses \(y_j\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) to minimize \(\sum_{j\in J}c_jy_j\), subject to \(\sum_{j:i\in E_j}x_{ij}=1\) for every \(i\in I\), \(x_{ij}=0\) when \(i\notin E_j\), and \(\sum_{i\in I}s_ix_{ij}\le C_jy_j\) for every \(j\in J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Costed bin packing opens candidate bins and assigns every item feasibly while minimizing total bin-opening cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Costed Bin Packing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The candidate-bin integer formulation is internally coherent, but no cited source establishes that this heterogeneous-capacity, eligibility-set formulation is the intended meaning of the leaf.

children.title: Capacity-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between available capacity choices and bin-selection costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto representation of installed-capacity versus opening-cost choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each feasible packing \(P\in\mathcal{P}\), let \(K(P)\) be the sum of capacities of its opened bins and \(C(P)\) their total cost. Its attainable outcome is \((K(P),C(P))\). The capacity-cost frontier is \(\mathcal{F}=\{(K(P),C(P)):P\in\mathcal{P},\ \nexists Q\in\mathcal{P}\text{ with }K(Q)\le K(P),\ C(Q)\le C(P)\text{ and at least one strict inequality}\}\). For any \(\lambda>0\), every minimizer of \(C(P)+\lambda K(P)\) is nondominated, although a discrete frontier point need not be obtained by any weighted-sum scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tradeoff frontier records feasible packings for which neither installed capacity nor opening cost can improve without worsening the other.
assumptions_latex: A fixed instance admits feasible packings using bins from a prescribed capacity-cost family.
Total installed capacity and total opening cost are both minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The capacity-cost frontier consists exactly of feasible nondominated pairs \((K(P),C(P))\).

notation.meaning: total installed capacity of packing P
total opening cost of packing P

children.title: Cardinality-Constrained Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Limits on the number of items per bin.

assumptions_latex: Items have sizes in \((0,1]\).
Every bin has unit capacity and may contain at most \(k\) items, where \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the smallest number of subsets satisfying both the unit-load and cardinality bounds.

notation.meaning: maximum number of items permitted in one bin
item set assigned to a bin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical identical-bin packing with a uniform item-count limit per bin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite item set \(I\), sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\), and an integer \(k\ge1\), a cardinality-constrained packing is a partition \(I=B_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_m\) such that, for every bin \(j\), both \(\sum_{i\in B_j}s_i\le1\) and \(|B_j|\le k\). The cardinality-constrained bin-packing problem is to minimize \(m\). Thus feasibility is governed simultaneously by total size and item count; neither constraint substitutes for the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the items into the fewest unit bins while limiting both total size and the number of items in every bin.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Constrained Bin Packing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard definition is precise and matches the terminal container, but the record supplies no source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Content-Compatibility Bin Family
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and diversity restrictions on bin contents.

children.title: Class-Constrained Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Bin-content restrictions expressed through item classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Class-Constrained Bin Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct-class-per-bin interpretation; other class-constrained conventions require separate sourcing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite item set with sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\), class map \(\kappa:I\to K\), and integer \(q\ge1\). A feasible class-constrained packing partitions \(I\) into bins \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in B_j}s_i\le1\) and \(|\{\kappa(i):i\in B_j\}|\le q\) for every \(j\). The objective is to minimize \(m\). The class restriction counts distinct represented classes, not the number of items belonging to each class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pack items into the fewest unit bins while permitting at most a specified number of distinct item classes in each bin.
assumptions_latex: Each item has a size in \((0,1]\) and belongs to exactly one class.
A bin may contain items from at most \(q\) distinct classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the minimum number of unit-capacity bins satisfying the load and distinct-class bounds.

children.title: Color-Constrained Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Diversity or multiplicity restrictions expressed through item colors.

assumptions_latex: Each item has a size in \((0,1]\) and one color.
No bin may contain two items of the same color.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the minimum number of unit-capacity bins satisfying capacity and color uniqueness.

notation.meaning: item set assigned to a bin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Same-color exclusion interpretation of colored bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite item set with sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\) and color map \(\chi:I\to C\). A color-constrained packing is a partition of \(I\) into bins \(B_1,ldots,B_m\) such that \(\sum_{i\in B_j}s_i\le1\) for every \(j\), and \(\chi(i)\ne\chi(i')\) whenever distinct items \(i,i'\) belong to the same bin. Equivalently, each color occurs at most once in each bin. The objective is to minimize \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pack items into the fewest unit bins while forbidding two items of the same color from sharing a bin.
knowledge_statements.title: Color-Constrained Bin Packing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The same-color exclusion model is internally precise, but “color-constrained bin packing” has multiple literature meanings and no source establishes this convention for the leaf.

children.title: Conflict-Constrained Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Compatibility restrictions expressed through prohibited item co-location.

assumptions_latex: Items have sizes in \((0,1]\).
An undirected graph records pairs of items forbidden to share a bin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the smallest number of independent sets whose loads are at most one and whose union partitions the vertices.

notation.meaning: item set assigned to a bin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-conflict version of identical unit-capacity bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an undirected graph \(G=(I,E)\) and sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\) for its vertices, a conflict-constrained packing partitions \(I\) into bins \(B_1,ldots,B_m\). Each bin must satisfy \(\sum_{i\in B_j}s_i\le1\) and must be an independent set of \(G\), meaning \(\{i,i'\}\notin E\) for every distinct \(i,i'\in B_j\). The conflict-constrained bin-packing problem minimizes \(m\). Capacity violations and graph conflicts are separate causes of infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertices representing items are partitioned into the fewest capacity-feasible independent sets of the conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Constrained Bin Packing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-conflict definition is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no source or specific locator is provided.

children.title: Adjacent Packing Generalizations
children.top_down_role: Close relatives retained as interfaces rather than geometric chapter expansions.

children.title: Vector Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Packing under several nonspatial capacity coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Bin Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nongeometric multidimensional packing with coordinatewise resource capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given vectors \(v_i=(v_{i1},\ldots,v_{id})\in[0,1]^d\) for a finite item set \(I\), a vector-bin packing is a partition \(I=B_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_m\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in B_j}v_i\le\mathbf{1}\) componentwise for every bin \(j\); equivalently, \(\sum_{i\in B_j}v_{ir}\le1\) for every coordinate \(r\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\). The vector bin-packing problem minimizes \(m\). Coordinates represent simultaneous nonspatial resources, so feasibility does not involve geometric placement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition demand vectors into the fewest bins so that every resource coordinate has total demand at most one in each bin.
assumptions_latex: The dimension \(d\ge1\) is fixed or supplied with the instance.
Each item vector lies in \([0,1]^d\), and bins have coordinatewise unit capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the minimum number of subsets whose coordinatewise vector sums do not exceed the all-ones vector.

children.title: Threshold-Filling Packing Duality
children.top_down_role: Threshold-filling counterparts of bin minimization.

children.title: Bin Covering
children.top_down_role: Threshold-filling problems centered on completed or covered bins.

assumptions_latex: Items have positive scalar sizes.
Each item is assigned to exactly one nonempty bin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the maximum number of bins whose total assigned size reaches the covering threshold.

notation.meaning: item set assigned to bin j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional identical-threshold bin covering with unrestricted overload.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite item set \(I\), sizes \(s_i>0\), and threshold \(L>0\), a bin-covering solution is a partition \(I=B_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_m\) into nonempty bins. Bin \(j\) is covered when \(\sum_{i\in B_j}s_i\ge L\). The objective is to maximize \(|\{j:\sum_{i\in B_j}s_i\ge L\}|\). Unlike bin packing, the threshold is a required lower bound rather than a capacity upper bound; loads above \(L\) remain feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition items to maximize the number of bins whose total size reaches a prescribed lower threshold; overfilling is allowed.
knowledge_statements.title: Bin Covering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-covering objective is coherent and fits the leaf, but no source supports the formulation. The unrestricted assumption \(s_i>0\), rather than the common normalized restriction \(s_i\le L\), particularly needs confirmation.

children.title: Dual Bin-Packing Variants
children.top_down_role: Packing counterparts formed by reversing the classical capacity objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Bin-Packing Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-maximizing dual bin packing with a fixed bin supply.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given item sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\) for \(i\in I\) and \(m\in\mathbb Z_{+}\) unit-capacity bins, dual bin packing selects a maximum-cardinality subset of items that can be packed into those bins. Equivalently, its value is
\[
\max\left\{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j=1}^{m}x_{ij}:\sum_{j=1}^{m}x_{ij}\le 1\ (i\in I),\ \sum_{i\in I}s_i x_{ij}\le1\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\ x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\right\}.
\]
Weighted variants replace the unit contribution of item \(i\) by a profit \(p_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed number of unit bins, choose the largest packable subset of items; weighted variants maximize the selected items’ total profit.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(s_i\in(0,1]\) for every \(i\in I\).
\(m\in\mathbb Z_{+}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed binary program equals the maximum number of items packable into the \(m\) bins.

notation.meaning: One when item i is assigned to bin j, and zero otherwise.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard cardinality-maximizing formulation of dual bin packing
A bin-packing-specific authoritative locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, formulation, and content kind fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the cardinality-maximizing or weighted variants.

children.title: Threshold-Filling Duality
children.top_down_role: The structural relation between bin minimization and threshold-filling objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Filling Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-and-objective reversal linking bin packing and bin covering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(\mathcal P\) of items with sizes \(s_i>0\), bin packing declares a block \(B\in\mathcal P\) feasible when \(\sum_{i\in B}s_i\le1\) and minimizes \(|\mathcal P|\). Bin covering declares a block covered when \(\sum_{i\in B}s_i\ge1\) and maximizes the number of covered blocks. Thus the threshold-filling correspondence reverses both the threshold inequality and the optimization direction. It is a structural duality between problem families, not in general the linear-programming duality of their standard formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Packing minimizes groups whose loads stay below capacity; covering maximizes groups whose loads reach a threshold. This is structural, not generally LP, duality.
assumptions_latex: The item set is finite.
\(s_i>0\) for every item \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The packing-to-covering correspondence is \((\le1,\min)\leftrightarrow(\ge1,\max)\).

notation.meaning: A partition of the item set into bins or blocks.

review_flags: A source explicitly distinguishing structural from linear-programming duality is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality content kind fits, but the structural-versus-LP-duality distinction lacks evidence. A source should also establish the intended item-size and leftover-item conventions for both problem families.

children.title: Geometric Container-Objective Boundary
children.top_down_role: Spatial placement variants routed to geometric packing.

children.title: Geometric Bin Packing
children.top_down_role: Spatial placement into fixed geometric containers.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Bin Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Axis-parallel two-dimensional geometric bin packing without rotations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given rectangles \(R_i=[0,w_i]\times[0,h_i]\) and identical bins \([0,W]\times[0,H]\), geometric bin packing asks for the least \(k\in\mathbb Z_{+}\) such that every rectangle can be translated into one of \(k\) bins, remains inside its assigned bin, and has interior disjoint from every other rectangle assigned there. In the axis-parallel, no-rotation version, translations preserve each rectangle's width \(w_i\) and height \(h_i\); touching boundaries is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pack all axis-parallel rectangles without overlap into the fewest identical rectangular bins; translations are allowed, rotations are not, and boundary contact is allowed.
assumptions_latex: The rectangle family is finite.
\(0<w_i\le W\) and \(0<h_i\le H\) for every item \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is the minimum number \(k\) of feasible \(W\)-by-\(H\) containers.

notation.meaning: Width and height of every bin.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard two-dimensional orthogonal geometric bin-packing definition
A geometric-packing source fixing rotation and boundary conventions is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but an authoritative source must support the axis-parallel, no-rotation, interior-disjointness, and boundary-contact conventions.

children.title: Geometric Strip Packing
children.top_down_role: Spatial placement into a strip with one extensible dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Strip Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Axis-parallel two-dimensional strip packing without rotations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given rectangles \(R_i=[0,w_i]\times[0,h_i]\) and a strip of fixed width \(W>0\), geometric strip packing minimizes a height \(H\ge0\) for which translations place every \(R_i\) inside \([0,W]\times[0,H]\) with pairwise interior-disjoint images. In the axis-parallel, no-rotation version, each translated rectangle retains width \(w_i\) and height \(h_i\). The optimum equals the least height of a horizontal line lying weakly above every placed rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Place all rectangles without overlap in a fixed-width strip while minimizing the occupied height; translations are allowed and rotations are forbidden.
assumptions_latex: The rectangle family is finite.
\(0<w_i\le W\) and \(h_i>0\) for every item \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum is \(\inf\{H\ge0:\text{a feasible placement in }[0,W]\times[0,H]\text{ exists}\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard two-dimensional orthogonal strip-packing definition
A geometric-packing source fixing rotation and boundary conventions is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source fixes the orientation, rotation, overlap, and boundary conventions or supports the stated objective characterization.

children.title: Container-Objective Boundary
children.top_down_role: The distinction between fixed-container minimization and variable-extent placement.

knowledge_statements.title: Container-Objective Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distinction between variable container count and variable container height.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed rectangle orientations, geometric bin packing fixes both container dimensions \((W,H)\) and minimizes the number of containers, whereas strip packing fixes only \(W\), uses one container, and minimizes \(H\). For any candidate height \(h\ge0\), a strip-packing instance has optimum at most \(h\) if and only if all its rectangles admit a nonoverlapping placement in the single container \([0,W]\times[0,h]\). This decision equivalence does not identify strip packing with multi-bin geometric bin packing, whose objective varies container multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bin packing varies the number of fixed-size containers; strip packing varies one container’s height. A guessed strip height yields a single-container feasibility test.
assumptions_latex: Rectangle orientations and the nonoverlap convention are fixed.
The strip width is \(W>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{strip}}\le h\) exactly when one \(W\)-by-\(h\) container is feasible.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct consequence of the standard geometric packing definitions
A source comparing geometric bin and strip objectives is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly targets the container-objective boundary, but the comparison and single-container decision equivalence have no inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Bin-Packing Representation-Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Compact, configuration, and network representations together with their associated certificates.

children.title: Bin-Packing Formulations
children.top_down_role: Representations used by exact and approximate algorithms.

children.title: Item-to-Bin Assignment Models
children.top_down_role: Compact indexed-bin formulations with bin symmetry.

knowledge_statements.title: Item-to-Bin Assignment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact indexed-bin integer formulation for one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For items \(i\in I\) of sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\), take \(M\ge |I|\) indexed unit bins. The compact assignment model is
\[
\min\sum_{j=1}^{M}y_j\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_{j=1}^{M}x_{ij}=1\ (i\in I),\qquad
\sum_{i\in I}s_i x_{ij}\le y_j\ (j=1,\ldots,M),
\]
with \(x_{ij},y_j\in\{0,1\}\). Every packing induces such a solution and conversely. Permuting bin indices produces equivalent solutions; constraints \(y_j\ge y_{j+1}\) may break part of this symmetry without changing the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary variables assign every item to one indexed bin and activate used bins. Bin-index permutations are symmetric, and ordered activation variables partially remove that symmetry.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(s_i\in(0,1]\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer program has the same optimum as one-dimensional unit-capacity bin packing.

notation.meaning: Valid upper bound on the number of bins.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard compact assignment formulation with bin symmetry
The supplied assignment references do not specifically support bin packing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and compact formulation fit the leaf, but the formulation-equivalence and symmetry-breaking claims require a bin-packing-specific source.

children.title: Implicit-Column Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Implicit-column formulations indexed by feasible bin contents.

children.title: Pattern-Indexed Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations indexed by feasible packing patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Indexed Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregated cutting-stock formulation indexed by feasible type-count patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let item type \(i\in T\) have size \(s_i\in(0,1]\) and integral demand \(b_i\). Define the feasible pattern set
\[
\mathcal P=\left\{a\in\mathbb Z_{+}^{T}:\sum_{i\in T}s_i a_i\le1\right\}.
\]
The pattern-indexed model is
\[
\min\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}z_a\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}a_i z_a\ge b_i\ (i\in T),\qquad z_a\in\mathbb Z_{+}.
\]
Each variable counts bins using one feasible pattern. Surplus pattern positions may be discarded, so covering demands is equivalent to packing exactly the required items.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each column is a feasible vector of item-type counts. Integer column multiplicities cover every demand while minimizing the number of bins.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite.
\(s_i\in(0,1]\) for all \(i\in T\).
\(b_i\in\mathbb Z_{+}\) for all \(i\in T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model's integer optimum equals the minimum number of unit-capacity bins for the aggregated instance.

notation.meaning: Number of type-i items in pattern a.

review_flags: A bin-packing or cutting-stock formulation source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pattern-indexed representation is standard and locally appropriate, but no cited cutting-stock or bin-packing source supports the formulation or the surplus-discard equivalence.

children.title: Configuration-Indexed Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations indexed by complete feasible bin configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration-Indexed Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-partitioning formulation indexed by feasible subsets of distinct items.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For distinct items \(I\) with sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\), let
\[
\mathcal C=\left\{C\subseteq I:\sum_{i\in C}s_i\le1\right\}.
\]
The configuration-indexed formulation is
\[
\min\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}z_C\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_{C\in\mathcal C:i\in C}z_C=1\ (i\in I),\qquad z_C\in\{0,1\}.
\]
A selected configuration is the item set placed in one bin. The equality constraints make selected configurations a partition of \(I\); allowing nonnegative integral \(z_C\) and covering inequalities gives an equivalent optimum after deleting duplicate or surplus item occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable selects a feasible subset of items as one bin. Selected subsets partition all items, and their number is minimized.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(s_i\in(0,1]\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected configurations encode exactly the feasible bin packings of \(I\).

notation.meaning: Indicator that configuration C is selected.

review_flags: A bin-packing-specific formulation source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The configuration-indexed representation fits the leaf, but the set-partitioning formulation and its claimed equivalence to the covering/integer variant lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Column-Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between pattern terminology and configuration-based columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of item configurations and aggregated type-count patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the distinct items \(I\) into types \(T	ilde{}\), where items of one type share a size, and let \(b_t\) be the multiplicity of type \(t\). Every feasible configuration \(C\subseteq I\) maps to the pattern \(a(C)\) defined by \(a_t(C)=|C\cap I_t|\). Conversely, every feasible pattern \(a\) satisfying \(a_t\le b_t\) can be realized by choosing \(a_t\) distinct items from each \(I_t\). Consequently, aggregating configuration columns with the same vector \(a(C)\) yields the pattern-indexed representation and preserves the integer packing optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counting each configuration’s items by type produces a pattern; every demand-bounded pattern can be lifted to distinct items. Aggregation preserves the integer optimum.
assumptions_latex: Items in each class \(I_t\) have a common size \(s_t\).
\(b_t=|I_t|\) for every type \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Configuration columns modulo item identities are exactly feasible demand-bounded pattern columns, with equal integer optimum.

notation.meaning: Set of distinct items of type t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct aggregation relation between pattern and configuration columns
A source explicitly establishing the aggregation equivalence is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but the aggregation-equivalence claim needs a source. The expression \(T\tilde{}\) is malformed or unexplained notation and should be corrected when a sourced version is prepared.

children.title: Network Configuration Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Network encodings of feasible configurations.

children.title: Arc-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Network formulations representing feasible packing through flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc-Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer arc-flow formulation on a capacity-state acyclic network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume integral item weights \(w_i\in\{1,\ldots,W\}\) and demands \(b_i\). Form a directed acyclic network with states \(0,
1,\ldots,W\), item arcs \((u,u+w_i,i)\) whenever \(u+w_i\le W\), and loss arcs permitting a partial load to reach \(W\). Send an integral flow of value \(z\) from \(0\) to \(W\), impose flow conservation at intermediate states, and require the total flow on arcs labeled \(i\) to equal \(b_i\). Minimizing \(z\) yields a bin-packing model: each integral source-to-sink flow path represents one feasible bin pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral flow paths through capacity states represent bins; labeled arcs place items and loss arcs represent unused capacity. Minimum source-to-sink flow equals the bin count.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb Z_{+}\).
\(w_i\in\{1,\ldots,W\}\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb Z_{+}\).
The network is acyclic and contains the stated item and loss arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing the integral \(0\)-to-\(W\) flow value produces the bin-packing optimum.

notation.meaning: Integral bin capacity and terminal state.
Source-to-sink flow value and number of bins.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard capacity-state arc-flow encoding of packing patterns
The supplied network-flow locators do not support the bin-packing construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but general network-flow references do not establish this packing construction. The exact loss-arc set and the resulting path-pattern correspondence require authoritative support.

children.title: State-Space Network Models
children.top_down_role: Networks whose nodes encode attainable packing states.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Network Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclic state-transition networks whose paths encode feasible bin configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state-space network for a packing formulation is a labeled directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,A)\) with source \(r\), sink \(t\), and a state map recording sufficient residual-resource information. Every \(r\)-to-\(t\) path must encode a feasible single-bin configuration through its multiset of item labels, and every admissible configuration must be encoded by at least one such path. Unlabeled or loss arcs may change the state without adding an item. Flow decomposition then converts any nonnegative integral \(r\)-to-\(t\) flow into a multiset of feasible configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: States record sufficient remaining resources, labeled transitions add items, and source-to-sink paths encode exactly the feasible single-bin configurations.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.
Every source-to-sink path has a well-defined item-label count vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The source-to-sink paths represent precisely the admissible single-bin configurations.
review_flags: The supplied general network-flow sources do not establish packing-state semantics.

children.title: Network-Compression Relation
children.top_down_role: Connections between state aggregation and compact arc-flow representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Compression Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-label preservation criterion for exact state-space compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be a state-space network and let \(G'\) be obtained by merging states and replacing arcs accordingly. If the merge preserves exactly the set
\[
\Lambda(G)=\left\{a(P):P\text{ is an }r\text{-to-}t\text{ path in }G\right\}
\]
of item-label count vectors, so that \(\Lambda(G')=\Lambda(G)\), then the path-column configuration model and the corresponding integral arc-flow model have the same feasible pattern multisets and objective values before and after compression. If merging creates a new source-to-sink label vector or deletes an old one, exact formulation equivalence can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State merging is exact when it preserves all and only source-to-sink item-count vectors. Creating or deleting such vectors can change the packing model.
assumptions_latex: Both networks have designated source and sink states.
Each source-to-sink path has an item-label count vector.
Compression preserves \(\Lambda(G)\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda(G')=\Lambda(G)\) implies equality of the induced configuration sets and packing optima.

notation.meaning: Item-label count vector of path P.
Set of label-count vectors represented by source-to-sink paths.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: representation equivalence follows from exact preservation of path-label vectors
A source for exact arc-flow network compression is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf and states a plausible exactness criterion, but a source is required to support the implication from preservation of label-count-vector sets to equivalence of the induced integral arc-flow formulations.

children.title: Bin-Packing Lower-Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial and relaxation-based lower bounds used for analysis and exact search.

children.title: Aggregate-Load Bound Family
children.top_down_role: Aggregate-load lower bounds.

children.title: Volume Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds derived from total item load relative to bin capacity.

assumptions_latex: There are finitely many items with sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\), where every bin has capacity \(C>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge \left\lceil \sum_{i=1}^n s_i/C\right\rceil\).

notation.meaning: minimum number of capacity-C bins needed to pack all items
total item volume normalized by bin capacity

review_flags: No bin-packing-specific authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The elementary aggregate-volume lower bound for one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any feasible packing into \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\) bins, summing the capacity constraints over all bins gives \(\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\le mC\). Consequently every feasible integer bin count satisfies \(m\ge \sum_{i=1}^n s_i/C\), and hence
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge \left\lceil\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n s_i}{C}\right\rceil.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The number of bins is at least the ceiling of total item size divided by bin capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Volume Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The volume bound is mathematically correct and the property kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The statement also includes a derivation rather than only the knowledge statement.

children.title: Continuous-Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Aggregate bounds obtained after relaxing discrete packing requirements.

assumptions_latex: There are finitely many items with sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\), and items may be split fractionally among capacity-\(C\) bins in the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fractional optimum is \(z_{\mathrm{frac}}=\sum_i s_i/C\), so \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge\lceil z_{\mathrm{frac}}\rceil\).

notation.meaning: minimum fractional number of bins when item mass is divisible

review_flags: No bin-packing-specific authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The divisible-load relaxation underlying the aggregate-volume bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the continuous relaxation, bin capacity is divisible and the total amount of purchased bin capacity may be fractional. Its optimal value is
\[
z_{\mathrm{frac}}=\frac{1}{C}\sum_{i=1}^n s_i,
\]
because exactly the aggregate item load must be covered. Every integral packing is feasible for this relaxation, so \(z_{\mathrm{frac}}\le \operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\). Since the integer optimum is integral,
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge \lceil z_{\mathrm{frac}}\rceil.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing divisible items yields fractional cost equal to normalized total load; rounding this value upward gives a valid integer lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Relaxation Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The divisible-load relaxation and its value are precise, and representation fits the container, but the record has no cited source and includes explanatory derivation.

children.title: Aggregate-Load Tightness
children.top_down_role: Instance regimes governing the strength of load-based certificates.

assumptions_latex: Items of sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\) admit a partition \(P_1,\ldots,P_L\) with \(\sum_{i\in P_b}s_i=C\) for every \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)=L=\left\lceil\sum_i s_i/C\right\rceil\).

notation.meaning: a partition block assigned to bin b
number of full blocks in the partition

review_flags: This is a sufficient tightness condition, not a characterization.
No bin-packing-specific authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition under which the aggregate-load lower bound is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the item set can be partitioned into \(L\) disjoint subsets \(P_1,\ldots,P_L\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in P_b}s_i=C\) for each \(b\in\{1,[31m1[0m\ldots,L\}\). These subsets define a packing into \(L\) bins, while their total load is \(LC\). Therefore the aggregate-load lower bound and this packing coincide:
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)=L=\frac{[31m1[0m\sum_{i=1}^n s_i}{C}=\left\lceil\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n s_i}{C}\right\rceil.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the items partition into exactly full bins, the volume lower bound equals the optimal bin count.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Load Tightness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated sufficient tightness condition is correct and condition is an appropriate kind, but the statement contains terminal escape artifacts and malformed mathematics, supplies no source, and includes proof-style reasoning.

children.title: Size-Distribution Bound Family
children.top_down_role: Bounds exploiting item-size distributions.

children.title: Large-Item Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds driven by items that sharply restrict bin cohabitation.

assumptions_latex: Items have sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\), and \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge\left\lceil |L_k|/k\right\rceil\).

notation.meaning: items larger than one (k+1)-st of a bin

review_flags: No bin-packing-specific authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-count bounds obtained from the maximum number of large items per bin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(L_k=\{i:s_i>C/(k+1)\}\). No capacity-\(C\) bin can contain \(k+1\) members of \(L_k\), since their combined size would exceed \(C\). Thus every bin contains at most \(k\) such items, and every feasible packing uses at least
\[
\left\lceil\frac{|L_k|}{k}\right\rceil
\]
bins. Hence \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge\lceil |L_k|/k\rceil\). In particular, items larger than \(C/2\) must occupy distinct bins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counting items above a size threshold gives a lower bound because only a limited number can share one bin.
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Item Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-count inequality is mathematically correct and property fits the leaf, but no authoritative source locator is supplied and the statement contains a derivation.

children.title: Cardinality Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds derived from limits on the number of items per bin.

assumptions_latex: Items have sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\).
A subset \(S\) and integer \(q\ge1\) satisfy \(\sum_{i\in T}s_i>C\) for every \(T\subseteq S\) with \(|T|=q+1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge\lceil |S|/q\rceil\).

notation.meaning: a distinguished subset whose members have bounded per-bin cardinality
maximum possible number of members of S in one bin

review_flags: No bin-packing-specific authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general subset-cardinality lower bound for bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume every \((q+1)\)-element subset \(T\subseteq S\) has \(\sum_{i\in T}s_i>C\). Then no feasible bin can contain more than \(q\) items from \(S\). If a packing uses \(m\) bins, it can accommodate at most \(mq\) members of \(S\), so \(|S|\le mq\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge [31m1[0m\left\lceil\frac{|S|}{q}\right\rceil.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each bin can contain at most q members of a chosen subset, at least the ceiling of its cardinality divided by q bins are required.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cardinality bound follows from the stated occupancy hypothesis and property fits the container, but the statement is corrupted by terminal escape text, contains proof material, and lacks a source.

children.title: Size-Class Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds obtained by grouping items into size ranges.

assumptions_latex: Items have sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\).
For \(j\ge1\), define the size class \(I_j=\{i:C/(j+1)<s_i\le C/j\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge\max_{j\ge1}\left\lceil |I_j|/j\right\rceil\).

notation.meaning: items in the j-th reciprocal size interval

review_flags: This record states the elementary per-class bound, not stronger mixed-class inequalities.
No bin-packing-specific authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reciprocal size classes yield simultaneous threshold-count lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each nonempty class \(I_j=\{i:C/(j+1)<s_i\le C/j\}\), a bin contains at most \(j\) members of \(I_j\), because \(j+1\) such items have total size greater than \(C\). Consequently every feasible packing requires at least \(\lceil |I_j|/j\rceil\) bins for each \(j\). Combining all classwise requirements gives
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge [31m1[0m\max_{j:I_j\ne\varnothing}\left\lceil\frac{|I_j|}{j}\right\rceil.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning items into reciprocal size intervals yields a lower bound from the occupancy limit of every nonempty class.
knowledge_statements.title: Size-Class Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The per-class bound is correct and appropriately scoped, but terminal escape text corrupts the displayed inequality, no source is cited, and the statement includes derivation.

children.title: Dual-Feasible-Function Bounds
children.top_down_role: Transformed-size lower-bound families.

assumptions_latex: Normalized item sizes satisfy \(x_i=s_i/C\in(0,1]\).
The function \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) satisfies \(\sum_{r=1}^p y_r\le1\Rightarrow\sum_{r=1}^p f(y_r)\le1\) for every finite sequence \(y_r\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)\ge\left\lceil\sum_i f(x_i)\right\rceil\).
review_flags: No authoritative locator specifically covering dual-feasible functions was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformed-size lower bounds for one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) is dual feasible when every finite sequence \(y_1,[31m1[0m\ldots,y_p\in[0,1]\) satisfying \(\sum_{r=1}^p y_r\le1\) also satisfies \(\sum_{r=1}^p f(y_r)\le1\). For normalized item sizes \(x_i=s_i/C\), the transformed sizes assigned to any feasible bin sum to at most one. Therefore a packing into \(m\) bins satisfies \(\sum_i f(x_i)\le m\), and
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(s,C)[31m1[0m\ge\left\lceil\sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i)\right\rceil.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any transformation preserving unit-bin feasibility converts total transformed size into a valid lower bound on the number of bins.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasible-Function Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual-feasible-function principle is mathematically standard and fits the transformed-size-bound topic, but the statement contains terminal escape artifacts and proof-style reasoning and has no authoritative source.

children.title: Configuration Primal-Dual Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Fractional configuration bounds and their dual interpretation.

children.title: Configuration-LP Bounds
children.top_down_role: Fractional lower bounds arising from configuration-based relaxations.

assumptions_latex: There are item types \(i=1,\ldots,t\) with sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\) and integer demands \(b_i\ge0\).
A configuration is any vector \(a\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^t\) satisfying \(\sum_i s_i a_i\le C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{conf}}=\min\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}x_a:\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}a_i x_a\ge b_i,\ x_a\ge0\}\le\operatorname{OPT}\), hence \(\lceil z_{\mathrm{conf}}\rceil\le\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: fractional multiplicity assigned to configuration a

review_flags: No authoritative bin-packing configuration-LP locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The covering configuration relaxation for typed one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A=\{a\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^t:\sum_{i=1}^t s_i a_i\le C\}\). The configuration relaxation is
\[
z_{\mathrm{conf}}=\min\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}x_a:\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}a_i x_a\ge b_i\ \text{for every }i,[31m1[0m\ x_a\ge0\right\}.
\]
An integral packing supplies an integral feasible vector of configuration multiplicities, so \(z_{\mathrm{conf}}\le\operatorname{OPT}\). Since \(\operatorname{OPT}\) is integral, \(\operatorname{OPT}\ge\lceil z_{\mathrm{conf}}\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The configuration LP fractionally selects feasible bin patterns to cover all demands; its rounded-up optimum lower-bounds the integer bin count.
knowledge_statements.title: Configuration-LP Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covering configuration LP is correctly formulated and representation fits the leaf, but its constraint display is corrupted, the text includes derivation, and no bin-packing configuration-LP source is supplied.

children.title: Dual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual witnesses supporting configuration-relaxation lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasible dual weighting certifies a numerical configuration-LP lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the covering configuration LP, a vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^t\) is a dual certificate if \(\sum_{i=1}^t a_i y_i\le 1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\). Its certified lower-bound value is \(\sum_{i=1}^t b_i y_i\), and it satisfies
\[
\sum_{i=1}^t b_i y_i\le z_{\mathrm{conf}}\le \operatorname{OPT}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative item-type weights whose total is at most one for every feasible bin configuration certify a lower bound equal to their demand-weighted sum.
assumptions_latex: The typed bin-packing instance has item types \(i=1,\ldots,t\), demands \(b_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\), and feasible configuration set \(\mathcal A\).
The vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^t\) satisfies \(\sum_{i=1}^t a_i y_i\le 1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^t b_i y_i\le z_{\mathrm{conf}}\le\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative dual weight assigned to item type i

children.title: Primal-Dual Bound Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The correspondence between fractional configurations and dual item valuations.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Bound Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LP duality applied to the configuration relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((P)\) be the covering configuration LP and \((D)\) its dual weighting program. If \((P)\) is feasible with finite optimum, finite-dimensional linear-programming duality yields
\[
z_{\mathrm{conf}}=\min(P)=\max(D)\le \operatorname{OPT}.
\]
Thus feasible dual solutions certify lower bounds, and an optimal dual solution attains the configuration-LP bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The configuration primal and dual have the same finite optimum, which lower-bounds the integer packing optimum; feasible dual solutions provide certificates for that bound.
assumptions_latex: The covering configuration LP \((P)\) is feasible and has a finite optimum.
The feasible configuration set \(\mathcal A\) is finite.
The program \((D)\) is the linear-programming dual of \((P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{conf}}=\min(P)=\max(D)\le\operatorname{OPT}\).

children.title: Online Fit Algorithms

children.title: Next Fit
children.top_down_role: The canonical one-open-bin policy.

assumptions_latex: Items arrive sequentially with sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\), and previously placed items cannot be moved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the packing formed by closing the current bin exactly when the next item does not fit.

notation.meaning: residual capacity of the unique open bin

review_flags: No authoritative online bin-packing algorithm locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The standard online Next Fit placement rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize one open bin with residual capacity \(r=C\). When item \(i\) of size \(s_i\) arrives, place it in the open bin if \(s_i\le r\), then update \(r\leftarrow r-s_i\). If \(s_i>r\), permanently close that bin, open a new bin, place item \(i\) there, and set \(r\leftarrow C-s_i\). After the final arrival, close the remaining open bin and output all bins created. At every time, at most one nonclosed bin is available for placement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Next Fit keeps one open bin; an item that does not fit closes it and starts a new bin.
knowledge_statements.title: Next Fit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm precisely states the canonical one-open-bin Next Fit policy, and algorithm is the correct kind, but no authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: First Fit
children.top_down_role: Earliest-feasible-bin placement.

assumptions_latex: Items arrive sequentially with sizes \(s_i\in(0,C]\), and previously placed items cannot be moved.
Bins are indexed by their opening order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each arriving item is assigned to the least-indexed bin with sufficient residual capacity, or to a newly opened bin if none exists.

notation.meaning: residual capacity of open bin j

review_flags: No authoritative online bin-packing algorithm locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The standard online First Fit placement rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize with no bins and \(m=0\). When item \(i\) of size \(s_i\) arrives, scan bins in increasing index order and choose
\[
j=[31m1[0m\min\{k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:r_k\ge s_i\}.
\]
If this set is nonempty, place item \(i\) in bin \(j\) and update \(r_j\leftarrow r_j-s_i\). Otherwise open bin \(m+1\), place the item there, set \(r_{m+1}=C-s_i\), and increment \(m\). After the final arrival, output the indexed bins and their assigned items.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First Fit places each arriving item in the earliest opened bin where it fits, opening a new bin only when necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: First Fit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic rule matches First Fit and algorithm is the correct kind, but the displayed least-index formula contains terminal escape corruption and no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Best Fit
children.top_down_role: Tightest-residual-capacity placement.

knowledge_statements.title: Best Fit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online Best Fit for one-dimensional unit-capacity bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given items arriving sequentially with sizes \(s_t\in(0,1]\), maintain opened bins with residual capacities \(r_b\). Initially no bin is open. On arrival of item \(t\), form \(F_t=\{b:r_b\ge s_t\}\). If \(F_t\ne\varnothing\), place the item in a bin \(b_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{b\in F_t}(r_b-s_t)\), breaking ties by a fixed rule, and update \(r_{b_t}\leftarrow r_{b_t}-s_t\). Otherwise open a new bin containing the item, with residual capacity \(1-s_t\). After the final arrival, output all opened bins and their assigned items.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Place each arriving item in a feasible open bin leaving the least residual capacity; if none exists, open a new bin.
assumptions_latex: \(s_t\in(0,1]\) for every arriving item.
Every bin has capacity \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a feasible packing determined without knowledge of future items.

notation.meaning: Residual capacity of open bin b.
Open bins feasible for arriving item t.

children.title: Harmonic Algorithm Family

knowledge_statements.title: Harmonic Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical \(k\)-class Harmonic online bin-packing family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer \(k\ge2\). Partition item sizes into \(I_j=(1/(j+1),1/j]\) for \(1\le j<k\) and \(I_k=(0,1/k]\). Maintain bins dedicated to a single class. An arriving item in \(I_j\), \(j<k\), is placed in the current class-\(j\) bin until that bin contains \(j\) items, after which a new class-\(j\) bin is opened. Items in \(I_k\) are packed by Next Fit within class \(k\): place the item in the current bin if feasible and otherwise close that bin and open another. Output all class-dedicated bins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Harmonic partitions sizes into reciprocal intervals and packs each class separately, limiting class-j bins to j items and using Next Fit for small items.
assumptions_latex: \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(k\ge2\).
Items arrive online with sizes in \((0,1]\), and bins have capacity \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every produced bin has total item size at most \(1\), and decisions use only the observed prefix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated Harmonic_k convention is plausible, but class-boundary and small-class conventions require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Refined Harmonic Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Template for refinements obtained by subdividing harmonic size classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0=a_0<a_1<\cdots<a_m=1\) define size classes \(C_i=(a_{i-1},a_i]\). A refined harmonic algorithm assigns each class \(C_i\) a finite collection \(P_i\) of admissible within-bin patterns and maintains at most a prescribed number of active bins of each pattern type. When an item of class \(C_i\) arrives, the algorithm places it into an active compatible pattern slot according to a fixed priority rule, or opens a bin of a permitted type. Feasibility requires \(\sum_i p_i a_i\le1\) for every pattern \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refined harmonic methods subdivide size intervals and use fixed feasible pattern and priority rules to exploit combinations suppressed by basic class separation.

Each permitted pattern satisfies the stated capacity inequality.

children.title: Super-Harmonic Families

knowledge_statements.title: Super-Harmonic Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract red-blue pattern template underlying Super-Harmonic online algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose finitely many size classes \(C_i=(a_{i-1},a_i]\), red fractions \(\alpha_i\in[0,1]\), and integer capacities \(\beta_i,\gamma_i\ge0\). Items of class \(i\) are designated online as blue or red so that the red count tracks \(\alpha_i\) times the class count up to a fixed discrepancy. A blue group contains at most \(\beta_i\) class-\(i\) items, a red group at most \(\gamma_i\), and groups may share a bin only through a predetermined compatible pair of group types whose maximum possible total size is at most \(1\). Unmatched groups occupy temporary bins; compatible groups are combined when the fixed policy permits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Super-Harmonic algorithms color class items red or blue in prescribed proportions and combine only preapproved compatible group types.
assumptions_latex: All class, fraction, capacity, compatibility, and tie-breaking parameters are fixed in advance.
Every compatible group pair has worst-case total size at most \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every bin created by the template is feasible, and its placement decisions are online.

notation.meaning: Target red fraction for class i.
Blue and red group capacities for class i.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairing-Policy Refinements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient capacity condition for pairing reserved groups across size classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a finite set of group types, and for each \(g\in G\) let \(u_g\in(0,1]\) be an upper bound on the total size of every realized group of type \(g\). Let \(E\subseteq G\times G\) specify the allowed pairings, and suppose an online matching rule matches each realized group at most once. If \(u_g+u_h\le 1\) for every \((g,h)\in E\), then placing each matched pair in one bin and each unmatched group alone produces a feasible packing. Different matching priorities may change the number of bins without invalidating this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficient feasibility certificate for a group-pairing policy is that the upper bounds of every allowed pair sum to at most one.
assumptions_latex: Each \(u_g\) upper-bounds the size of every realized group of type \(g\).
Each realized group is matched at most once.
Every unmatched group is placed alone in a unit-capacity bin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(u_g+u_h\le 1\) for every \((g,h)\in E\), every packing produced by the stated pairing policy is feasible.

notation.meaning: Upper bound on the size of a realized group of type g.

knowledge_statements.title: First Fit Decreasing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline First Fit applied after nonincreasing size sorting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite instance \(I=(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) with \(s_i\in(0,1]\), choose a permutation \(\pi\) such that \(s_{\pi(1)}\ge\cdots\ge s_{\pi(n)}\), breaking equal-size ties deterministically. Start with an empty ordered list of bins. For \(t=1,\ldots,n\), scan the existing bins in opening order and place item \(\pi(t)\) in the first bin whose current load plus \(s_{\pi(t)}\) is at most \(1\). If no existing bin is feasible, append a new bin containing that item. After all items are processed, output the ordered bins; this packing is denoted \(\operatorname{FFD}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort the finite instance by nonincreasing item size, then place each item in the earliest opened bin where it fits, opening a new bin if necessary.
assumptions_latex: The instance is \(I=(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) with \(n<\infty\) and \(s_i\in(0,1]\) for every \(i\).
Every bin has capacity \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{FFD}(I)\) is a feasible offline bin packing of \(I\).

notation.meaning: Permutation ordering the items by nonincreasing size.

knowledge_statements.title: Best Fit Decreasing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline Best Fit applied after nonincreasing size sorting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite instance \(I=(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) with \(s_i\in(0,1]\), choose a permutation \(\pi\) satisfying \(s_{\pi(1)}\ge\cdots\ge s_{\pi(n)}\), with a fixed rule for equal-size ties. Initially no bin is open. For \(t=1,\ldots,n\), let \(F_t\) be the set of open bins whose residual capacity is at least \(s_{\pi(t)}\). If \(F_t\ne\varnothing\), place item \(\pi(t)\) in a bin in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{b\in F_t}(r_b-s_{\pi(t)})\), using a fixed tie rule, where \(r_b\) is the residual capacity before placement. Otherwise open a new bin containing the item. The resulting packing is denoted \(\operatorname{BFD}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort the finite instance by nonincreasing item size, then place each item in a feasible bin that leaves the least residual capacity, opening a new bin when none is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The instance is \(I=(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) with \(n<\infty\) and \(s_i\in(0,1]\) for every \(i\).
Every bin has capacity \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BFD}(I)\) is a feasible offline bin packing of \(I\).

notation.meaning: Permutation ordering the items by nonincreasing size.
Open bins feasible for the t-th sorted item.

knowledge_statements.title: Fernández de la Vega-Lueker Grouping Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear grouping and rounding framework for an asymptotic bin-packing scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(varepsilon\in(0,1)\). Separate an instance \(I\) into large items \(L=\{i:s_i\gevarepsilon\}\) and small items \(S=I\setminus L\). Sort \(L\) nonincreasingly and partition it consecutively into \(q=O(1/varepsilon^2)\) groups of nearly equal cardinality. Set aside the first group and, in every later group, round each size upward to the largest size in that group. Enumerate or optimize the finitely many feasible configurations of rounded large-item types, restore the set-aside items using extra bins, and insert small items greedily into residual capacity. Output the best packing obtained under the framework's configuration choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group sorted large items, round within groups, optimize the resulting constant-type instance, and greedily insert small items, allowing an additive number of bins.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite unit-capacity bin-packing instance.
\(varepsilon\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With suitable group sizes and configuration optimization, the framework yields \(operatorname{ALG}(I)le(1+O(varepsilon))operatorname{OPT}(I)+O(1/varepsilon^2)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum number of bins for instance I.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gilmore-Gomory configuration LP for typed one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let item types \(i=1,\ldots,m\) have sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\) and demands \(b_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\). Define \(\mathcal{C}=\{a\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^m:\sum_{i=1}^m a_i s_i\le1\}\). With a variable \(x_a\ge0\) for every \(a\in\mathcal{C}\), the configuration relaxation is \[\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}=\min\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal{C}}x_a:\sum_{a\in\mathcal{C}}a_i x_a\ge b_i\ \text{for every }i=1,\ldots,m,\quad x_a\ge0\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal{C}\right\}.\] Every packing induces an integral feasible vector, and every integral feasible vector specifies enough feasible configurations to pack the demanded items; consequently \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}\le\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The configuration LP fractionally selects feasible single-bin patterns whose aggregate item multiplicities cover every type demand.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many item types with \(s_i\in(0,1]\).
Every demand satisfies \(b_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}\le\operatorname{OPT}\), and requiring \(x_a\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) for every \(a\in\mathcal{C}\) gives the pattern-based integer formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Relaxation Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate configuration-LP optimization through dual separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the configuration LP with demands \(b_i\), form its dual \[maxleft{sum_i b_i y_i:y_ige0,quadsum_i a_i y_ile1text{ for every }ainmathcal Cright}.\] Given a candidate \(y\), invoke a knapsack oracle maximizing \(sum_i a_i y_i\) subject to \(ainmathcal C\). A returned value greater than \(1\) supplies a violated dual constraint; otherwise the oracle certifies separation, exactly or within its stated tolerance. Apply an ellipsoid or column-generation procedure using these configurations, terminate at the requested objective tolerance, and recover a primal fractional configuration vector supported on the generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the exponentially large configuration LP by finding violated dual constraints with a knapsack oracle and retaining only generated configurations.
assumptions_latex: Item sizes and demands are rationally encoded.
The knapsack oracle has a specified exact or approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact separation gives exact rational LP optimization; approximate separation gives a relaxation solution whose objective loss is controlled by the oracle tolerance.

Configuration returned by the knapsack oracle.

children.title: Optimization-Accuracy Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy conventions for feasible approximate solutions of the configuration relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}>0\), and let \(\widehat{x}\) be a feasible configuration-LP solution with value \(\widehat{z}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{C}}\widehat{x}_a\). For parameters \(\delta\ge0\) and \(\eta\ge0\), additive accuracy means \(\widehat{z}\le z^*+\delta\), relative accuracy means \(\widehat{z}\le(1+\eta)z^*\), and mixed accuracy means \(\widehat{z}\le(1+\eta)z^*+\delta\). Relative accuracy bounds the additive objective error by \(\eta z^*\), while additive accuracy bounds the relative objective error by \(\delta/z^*\). These bounds concern relaxation optimization only and do not include subsequent rounding loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible configuration-LP solution can be measured by additive, relative, or mixed objective accuracy; conversions depend on the positive LP optimum and exclude later rounding loss.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat{x}\) is feasible for the configuration relaxation.
\(z^*=\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}>0\).
\(\eta,\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\widehat{z}\le z^*+\delta\), \(\widehat{z}\le(1+\eta)z^*\), and \(\widehat{z}\le(1+\eta)z^*+\delta\) specify additive, relative, and mixed optimization accuracy, respectively.

notation.meaning: Objective value of the computed solution.

children.title: Rounding Components

assumptions_latex: Items have sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\), and a configuration is a vector \(a\in\mathbb Z_+^n\) satisfying \(\sum_i a_i s_i\le 1\).
A fractional configuration solution \(x\ge 0\) satisfies \(\sum_a a_i x_a\ge 1\) for every item type \(i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose integral multiplicities \(z_a\in\mathbb Z_+\) and residual multiplicities \(r_a\ge 0\) such that \(x_a=z_a+r_a\) for every configuration \(a\). The integral part directly opens \(\sum_a z_a\) bins. Its covered multiplicity for item type \(i\) is \(c_i=\sum_a a_i z_a\), and the uncovered demand is \(d_i=(1-c_i)_+\). A valid rounding component supplies a residual packing procedure producing configurations \(y\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal C}\) with \(\sum_a a_i y_a\ge d_i\) for all \(i\), while controlling \(\sum_a y_a\) by a stated function of the residual structure.

children.title: Discrepancy Components
children.top_down_role: Balancing components controlling losses during integral recovery.

assumptions_latex: The residual incidence matrix is \(A\in\mathbb Z_+^{m\times q}\), and \(x\in[0,1]^q\) is a fractional column vector.
A rounding vector \(z\in\{0,1\}^q\) is chosen for the residual columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(A(z-x)\) measures item-type coverage error, and a discrepancy bound controls the demand left for repair.
review_flags: The intended discrepancy theorem and norm bound are not identified.
No relevant bin-packing or discrepancy source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrepancy is stated as the coverage-error interface used by an integral-recovery argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every item type \(i\), define the signed coverage error by \(\Delta_i=(A(z-x))_i\). If the discrepancy component guarantees \(\|A(z-x)\|_\infty\le D\), then rounding changes the coverage of each type by at most \(D\). In particular, whenever \(Ax\ge d\), the rounded selection satisfies \(Az\ge d-D\mathbf 1\). Thus only the deficit vector \(u=(d-Az)_+\) must be passed to the residual packing procedure, and it obeys \(0\le u_i\le D\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-discrepancy rounding limits each item type's coverage loss, leaving a componentwise bounded deficit for residual packing.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrepancy Components

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise deficit implication is mathematically consistent and the property kind fits the container. However, the existence, value, and applicable hypotheses of the asserted discrepancy bound are left conditional and unsupported by a cited result.

children.title: Integral-Recovery Interface

assumptions_latex: A fractional configuration solution and its rounded integral configuration multiset are given.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integral recovery is valid exactly when the returned residual configurations cover \(d\); the resulting bin count is the sum of rounded and repair configurations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The integral-recovery interface accepts \((z,d)\), where \(z\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal C}\) is the rounded configuration vector and \(d\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) is its uncovered demand. It returns \(y\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal C}\). The output is a verifiable recovery certificate when \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal C}a_i y_a\ge d_i\) for every type \(i\). Under this condition, \(z+y\) covers the original item multiplicities, hence encodes a feasible packing using exactly \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal C}(z_a+y_a)\) bins. Any claimed additive recovery loss is certified by separately checking the asserted upper bound on \(\sum_a y_a\).
