children.title: Stage-Structured Cutting Family
children.top_down_role: Structured spatial cutting routed to geometric packing.

children.title: Guillotine Cutting
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional cutting restricted to edge-to-edge cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Guillotine Cutting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive axis-parallel guillotine separability for rectangular stock.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be an axis-parallel rectangle containing finitely many pairwise interior-disjoint rectangular items. A layout is guillotine-cuttable if either it contains at most one item, or there exists a horizontal or vertical line segment joining two opposite sides of \(B\), intersecting no item interior, such that the segment partitions \(B\) into two rectangles whose induced item layouts are both guillotine-cuttable. The resulting recursive partition defines a guillotine cutting sequence; every cut traverses the entire current rectangular subpiece.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rectangular layout is guillotine-cuttable when recursive full-width or full-height cuts can isolate all items without crossing an item interior.
assumptions_latex: The stock and all items are axis-parallel rectangles.
Item interiors are pairwise disjoint and contained in the stock.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\text{ is guillotine-cuttable}\iff B\text{ admits the stated recursive full-span partition}.\)
review_flags: No supplied source locator concerns guillotine cutting.
A cutting-stock reference should confirm whether boundary-touching and trim-loss conventions alter the definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive definition and content kind fit guillotine cutting, but no inspectable source establishes the precise full-span, rectangular-item, and boundary-contact conventions.

children.title: Multistage Cutting
children.top_down_role: Cutting layouts organized into a bounded or prescribed sequence of stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Cutting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stage-bounded guillotine cutting with one orientation shared within each stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A guillotine cutting plan for a rectangular stock sheet is a \(k\)-stage plan if its cuts can be partitioned into ordered nonempty stages \(1,\ldots,k\) such that all cuts in a stage are mutually parallel, consecutive stages use perpendicular orientations, and every cut in stage \(s\) is applied to a subrectangle created by stages earlier than \(s\). Cuts within the same stage may be performed independently on distinct current subrectangles. A layout is at-most-\(k\)-stage cuttable when some such plan using no more than \(k\) stages separates its required items.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage plan groups full-span cuts into alternating horizontal and vertical stages, with later cuts acting on pieces created earlier.
assumptions_latex: All cuts are guillotine cuts on rectangular current pieces.
A fixed integer stage limit \(k\ge1\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{layout is at-most-}k\text{-stage cuttable}\iff\text{an admissible plan with at most }k\text{ stages exists}.\)
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses multistage guillotine cutting.
Stage conventions vary regarding exact versus maximum stage count and normalization of redundant stages.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but stage-count and within-stage dependency conventions vary. A directly relevant source is required to establish this particular formulation.

children.title: Stage-Structure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Layout classes distinguished by permissible cut orientations and stage organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Structure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment relations among exact-stage, bounded-stage, and unrestricted guillotine layout classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed rectangular instance, let \(\mathcal{G}_{\le k}\) denote the layouts admitting a guillotine plan with at most \(k\) alternating-orientation stages, and let \(\mathcal{G}\) denote all guillotine-cuttable layouts. Then \(\mathcal{G}_{\le1}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_{\le2}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal{G}\). If \(\mathcal{G}_{=k}=\mathcal{G}_{\le k}\setminus\mathcal{G}_{\le k-1}\) for \(k\ge2\), with \(\mathcal{G}_{=1}=\mathcal{G}_{\le1}\), the exact-stage classes are pairwise disjoint and their union is \(\mathcal{G}\) whenever every finite guillotine tree has a finite stage decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing more stages cannot remove feasible layouts; minimum-stage classes partition the finite guillotine layouts.
assumptions_latex: Layouts contain finitely many items and admit finite cutting trees.
Consecutive stages alternate cut orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{G}_{\le k}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_{\le k+1}\subseteq\mathcal{G}\) and \(\mathcal{G}=\biguplus_{k\ge1}\mathcal{G}_{=k}\).

notation.meaning: layouts requiring at most k stages
layouts whose minimum stage count is k

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports the stage-regime hierarchy.
The claim depends on the adopted stage-decomposition convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the correct role for the regime containments, but the partition claim depends on the adopted stage definition and finite-stage decomposition convention, neither of which is sourced.

children.title: General Geometric-Layout Boundary
children.top_down_role: General layout and irregular-shape cutting routed to geometric packing.

children.title: Nonguillotine Cutting
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional cutting without a guillotine-layout restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonguillotine Cutting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular layouts not separable by recursive full-span cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be an axis-parallel rectangular stock region containing finitely many pairwise interior-disjoint items. A feasible layout is nonguillotine if no recursive sequence of horizontal or vertical full-span cuts can separate all required items without some cut intersecting an item interior. Equivalently, the layout has no guillotine cutting tree whose leaves contain the individual items. The designation concerns the realized layout: an instance may possess both guillotine and nonguillotine feasible layouts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible layout is nonguillotine when its items cannot all be separated by recursive full-span horizontal or vertical cuts.
assumptions_latex: The stock is rectangular and item interiors are pairwise disjoint.
Cuts must avoid item interiors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{layout is nonguillotine}\iff\text{no valid guillotine cutting tree exists}.\)
review_flags: No supplied source locator concerns nonguillotine layouts.
A geometric cutting reference should confirm whether the intended scope permits nonrectangular items.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly expresses nonguillotine status relative to the preceding guillotine notion, but no source confirms its restriction to rectangular stock, axis-parallel cuts, or the intended item-shape scope.

children.title: Nesting Problems
children.top_down_role: Placement of irregular pieces within stock material.

knowledge_statements.title: Nesting Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional placement formulation for irregular or rectangular pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a stock region \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\), piece shapes \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\) for \(i\in I\), and allowed rigid transformations \(T_i\), a nesting solution selects transformations \(t_i\in T_i\) such that \(t_i(P_i)\subseteq S\) for every selected piece and \(\operatorname{int}(t_i(P_i))\cap\operatorname{int}(t_j(P_j))=\varnothing\) whenever \(i\ne j\). The optimization problem minimizes required stock, waste, or used extent, or maximizes the value of selected pieces, subject to these containment and nonoverlap conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nesting places transformed shapes inside stock without interior overlap while optimizing stock use, waste, extent, or selected value.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_i\) and \(S\) is a closed measurable planar region.
Each allowed transformation set \(T_i\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_i(P_i)\subseteq S\) and \(\operatorname{int}(t_i(P_i))\cap\operatorname{int}(t_j(P_j))=\varnothing\) for all \(i\ne j\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses geometric nesting.
The objective and admissible transformations vary across nesting-problem variants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition broadly fits nesting problems, but objectives and admissible transformations vary by variant. It also refers to selected pieces without defining the selected index set, while the conclusion quantifies over all items.

children.title: Geometric-Layout Boundary
children.top_down_role: The transition from cutting-stock allocation to general spatial layout.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Layout Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where scalar cutting patterns cease to characterize geometric feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let item \(i\) have planar shape \(P_i\), and let \(a_i\) be its area. For stock region \(S\), the aggregate condition \(\sum_i a_i\le\operatorname{area}(S)\) is necessary for a nonoverlapping layout but is not sufficient. For example, two axis-parallel squares of side \(2\) have total area \(8\), equal to the area of a rectangle of dimensions \(1\) by \(8\), yet neither square fits in that stock. Thus a cutting-stock representation based only on scalar resource consumption crosses into a geometric-layout problem when containment, orientation, or pairwise nonoverlap must be modeled explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Area or other scalar capacity alone does not ensure a feasible layout; containment, orientation, and nonoverlap mark the geometric boundary.
assumptions_latex: Pieces must lie inside the stock without interior overlap.
The example forbids rotation from changing square dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i a_i\le\operatorname{area}(S)\not\Rightarrow\text{geometric feasibility}.\)
review_flags: No supplied source locator documents the cutting-stock versus geometric-layout boundary.
The counterexample is elementary, but the intended taxonomy boundary needs source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct content kind, and the area counterexample is mathematically valid. However, no cited source supports the broader claimed boundary between scalar cutting-stock representations and geometric-layout models.

children.top_down_role: Item-oriented, pattern-oriented, and network representations ordered before their solution methods.

children.title: Compact Direct-Index Model Family
children.top_down_role: Direct formulations using stock copies, assignments, or positions.

children.title: Item-Indexed Assignment Models
children.top_down_role: Compact formulations organized around item assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Item-Indexed Assignment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact assignment formulation for one-dimensional bin packing or unit-demand cutting stock.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let items \(i\in I\) have lengths \(a_i>0\), and let identical stock copies \(j\in J\) have capacity \(L>0\), with \(|J|\ge|I|\). Binary variable \(x_{ij}\) assigns item \(i\) to copy \(j\), and \(y_j\) activates copy \(j\). A compact model is \[\min\sum_{j\in J}y_j\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{j\in J}x_{ij}=1\ \ (i\in I),\quad\sum_{i\in I}a_i x_{ij}\le Ly_j\ \ (j\in J),\quad x_{ij},y_j\in\{0,1\}.\] Its integer feasible solutions correspond to assignments of every item to a capacity-feasible used stock copy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary variables assign each item to one used stock copy, while capacity constraints ensure that every copy can contain its assigned lengths.
assumptions_latex: Every item is required once and satisfies \(0<a_i\le L\).
The candidate-copy set \(J\) is large enough to hold all items.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\sum_{j\in J}y_j\) represents the minimum number of identical stock copies used.
review_flags: Supplied assignment-problem locators do not support this capacity-constrained cutting-stock formulation.
A bin-packing or cutting-stock formulation source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is a standard item-indexed bin-packing formulation and fits the leaf, but the inventory contains only ordinary assignment-problem sources, which do not support its activation and capacity formulation.

children.title: Stock-Copy Models
children.top_down_role: Compact formulations using explicit copies of available stock.

knowledge_statements.title: Stock-Copy Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-index formulation with one variable block for each candidate stock copy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let stock copies \(j\in J\) have capacities \(L_j>0\) and costs \(c_j\ge0\), and let item type \(i\in I\) have length \(a_i>0\) and integer demand \(b_i\ge0\). Integer variable \(z_{ij}\) counts type-\(i\) items cut from copy \(j\), while binary \(y_j\) indicates use. The stock-copy model is \[\min\sum_{j\in J}c_jy_j\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{j\in J}z_{ij}\ge b_i\ \ (i\in I),\quad\sum_{i\in I}a_i z_{ij}\le L_jy_j\ \ (j\in J),\quad z_{ij}\in\mathbb{Z}_{+},\ y_j\in\{0,1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each candidate stock copy has usage and item-count variables; demand couples copies, and a capacity constraint governs every used copy.
assumptions_latex: Items and stock are one-dimensional, and kerf is absent or included in \(a_i\).
The finite set \(J\) contains enough stock copies to satisfy demand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer feasible solutions encode demand-covering cutting plans indexed directly by stock copy.

notation.meaning: number of type-i items cut from stock copy j

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports a stock-copy cutting formulation.
Demand equality versus covering and symmetry-breaking conventions require source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct role and the model is coherent, but no source supports this stock-copy formulation or its demand-covering rather than exact-demand convention.

children.title: Position-Indexed Models
children.top_down_role: Compact formulations organized around cutting or placement positions.

knowledge_statements.title: Position-Indexed Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-coordinate formulation for one-dimensional nonoverlapping placement on candidate stock copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume integral item lengths \(a_i\) and stock length \(L\). For candidate copies \(j\in J\) and start coordinates \(p\in\{0,\ldots,L-a_i\}\), let binary \(x_{ijp}=1\) mean item \(i\) starts at position \(p\) on copy \(j\); let \(y_j\) indicate use. Impose \(\sum_{j,p}x_{ijp}=1\) for every item and, for every \(j\) and unit coordinate \(q\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\), impose \(\sum_{i,p:\,p\le q<p+a_i}x_{ijp}\le y_j\). Minimizing \(\sum_j y_j\) yields a discrete position-indexed model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each item chooses a stock copy and integer start position; coordinate-occupancy constraints prevent overlap and activate every used copy.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and all \(a_i\) are positive integers with \(a_i\le L\).
Items cannot overlap and every item must be placed once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary feasible solutions are exactly the nonoverlapping integer-coordinate placements on the candidate stock copies.

notation.meaning: indicator that item i starts at position p on copy j
unit stock coordinate covered by an item

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports position-indexed cutting-stock models.
The discretization and half-open occupancy convention require a directly relevant source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits position-indexed models and is internally consistent under integral coordinates, but no source supports the discretization, occupancy constraints, or claimed exact correspondence.

children.title: Gilmore-Gomory Pattern Model

children.title: Pattern Covering Master
children.top_down_role: Pattern assembly under demand-covering rows.

assumptions_latex: There are finitely many item types with demands \(d_i\in\mathbb Z_+\).
The pattern set \(P\) is finite, and each pattern column \(a^p\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) is feasible for one stock object.
Every demanded item type occurs in at least one pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal value is the minimum number of stock objects whose selected patterns cover all demands.

notation.meaning: Number of copies of pattern p
Number of items of type i produced by pattern p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer Gilmore-Gomory master with unit cost per stock object and permitted overproduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given patterns \(P\), demands \(d\in\mathbb Z_+^m\), and pattern columns \(a^p\in\mathbb Z_+^m\), the pattern-covering master is
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P}x_p:\ \sum_{p\in P}a_i^p x_p\ge d_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\quad x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\quad(p\in P)\right\}.
\]
Its linear relaxation replaces \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\) by \(x_p\ge0\). A feasible integer vector specifies a multiset of stock-cutting patterns whose aggregate output covers every demand row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose nonnegative integer pattern multiplicities minimizing the number of stock objects while producing at least the demand of every item type.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Covering Master

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unit-cost integer covering representation is mathematically precise and fits the Pattern Covering Master container, but no inspectable source supports the cutting-stock formulation.

children.title: Exact-Demand Pattern Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Pattern masters requiring exact fulfillment of demand.

assumptions_latex: The pattern matrix is \(A=(a_i^p)\in\mathbb Z_+^{m\times |P|}\).
The demand vector satisfies \(d\in\mathbb Z_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible solutions produce exactly \(d_i\) units of every item type \(i\), with no overproduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-output integer variant of the pattern master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The exact-demand pattern-partitioning master is
\[
\min\left\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}x:\ Ax=d,\quad x\in\mathbb Z_+^{|P|}\right\}.
\]
Thus each demand row is an equality rather than a covering inequality. Its linear relaxation uses \(x\in\mathbb R_+^{|P|}\). Exact-demand feasibility is not implied by feasibility of the covering master because surplus output cannot be discarded in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select integer pattern multiplicities of minimum total count so aggregate production equals, rather than merely covers, every demand.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Demand Pattern Partitioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-output formulation and its distinction from covering are coherent and fit this variant container, but the record has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines feasible one-dimensional cutting patterns and distinguishes the exact-demand integer model from its displayed linear-programming relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) satisfy \(w_i\le W\), and let \(b_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). A feasible pattern is a vector \(A_j=(a_{1j},\ldots,a_{mj})^\top\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i a_{ij}\le W\). If \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) enumerate all feasible patterns, the exact-demand integer model is \[\min\left\{\sum_{j=1}^n x_j:\ \sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}x_j=b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n\right\}.\] Replacing \(x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n\) by \(x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n\) gives the linear-programming relaxation displayed in the source.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible cutting pattern is a nonnegative integer vector whose total width does not exceed the stock-roll width. Enumerating all feasible patterns gives an exact-demand integer model minimizing the number of stock rolls; allowing real nonnegative pattern multiplicities gives its LP relaxation.
assumptions_latex: W\in\mathbb Z_{>0}
w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\quad w_i\le W\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
b_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
A_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m,\quad \sum_{i=1}^m w_i a_{ij}\le W

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The bounded-overproduction pattern master is
\[
\min\left\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}x:\ d\le Ax\le d+u,\quad x\in\mathbb Z_+^{|P|}\right\},
\]
where both vector inequalities are componentwise. The special choice \(u=0\) gives exact-demand partitioning; omitting the upper inequalities gives the covering master. Its linear relaxation replaces integer multiplicities by nonnegative real multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the number of selected patterns while meeting demand and limiting each item type's surplus by a prescribed amount.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise bounded-overproduction formulation is precise and correctly specializes to exact demand when u=0, but it lacks source support.

children.title: Output-Policy Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Feasibility effects arising from stricter output policies.

assumptions_latex: The available pattern columns are \(a^p\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) for \(p\in P\).
The output policy is the interval \([d,d+u]\) with \(d,u\in\mathbb Z_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy is integer-feasible exactly when \(M(P)\cap[d,d+u]\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Integer monoid generated by available pattern columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility boundary for finite-pattern integer output policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
M(P)=\left\{\sum_{p\in P}a^p x_p:x\in\mathbb Z_+^{|P|}\right\}.
\]
The bounded-output policy \(d\le Ax\le d+u\) is feasible if and only if
\[
M(P)\cap\{y\in\mathbb Z_+^m:d\le y\le d+u\}\ne\varnothing.
\]
Consequently, exact-demand feasibility is the boundary case \(d\in M(P)\), whereas unrestricted covering asks whether some \(y\in M(P)\) satisfies \(y\ge d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An output policy is feasible exactly when its permitted output box intersects the integer monoid generated by the available patterns.
knowledge_statements.title: Output-Policy Feasibility Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monoid-intersection condition is an exact restatement of integer feasibility and fits the feasibility-boundary container, but no source is supplied for this framing.

assumptions_latex: The covering master is relaxed to \(\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\ge0\}\).
The data satisfy \(A\ge0\) and \(d\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A demand-price vector is dual feasible precisely when \(\pi\ge0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\pi\le\mathbf1\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative dual prices of demand-covering rows

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linear-programming dual of
\[
\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\ge0\}
\]
is
\[
\max\{d^{\mathsf T}\pi:A^{\mathsf T}\pi\le\mathbf1,\ \pi\ge0\}.
\]
Thus \(\pi_i\) assigns a nonnegative marginal value to one unit of item-type demand, while each pattern \(p\) must satisfy \(\sum_i a_i^p\pi_i\le1\). For any primal- and dual-feasible pair, weak duality gives \(d^{\mathsf T}\pi\le\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand prices are nonnegative dual variables whose total value on every pattern cannot exceed that pattern's unit stock cost.

children.title: Pattern Reduced-Cost Valuation
children.top_down_role: Economic valuation of candidate cutting patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Reduced-Cost Valuation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced cost and full-master LP optimality test under unit stock-object cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\subseteq P\) be the current restricted pattern set, let \(x^R\) be an optimal solution of its unit-cost master LP, and let \(\pi\ge 0\) be an associated optimal dual vector. For any full-master pattern \(p\in P\) with column \(a^p\), its reduced cost is
\[
\bar c_p=1-(a^p)^{\mathsf T}\pi=1-\sum_{i=1}^m a_i^p\pi_i.
\]
Thus \(p\) has negative reduced cost exactly when \((a^p)^{\mathsf T}\pi>1\). If every \(p\in P\) satisfies \(\bar c_p\ge 0\), then \(\pi\) is feasible for the full-master dual and \(x^R\), extended by zero on \(P\setminus R\), is optimal for the full-master linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an optimal restricted-master primal-dual pair, a pattern's reduced cost is one minus its dual-valued output. A negative value identifies an improving candidate column, while nonnegative reduced costs for every full-master pattern certify full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted pattern set satisfies \(R\subseteq P\), where \(P\) is the full feasible pattern set.
The restricted-master primal solution \(x^R\) and its associated dual vector \(\pi\ge0\) are optimal.
Every pattern has unit master cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(p\in P\), \(\bar c_p=1-(a^p)^{\mathsf T}\pi\); if \(\bar c_p\ge0\) for all \(p\in P\), then the restricted-master optimum is also a full-master LP optimum.

The pricing set \(P\) contains every feasible cutting pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted master is full-master optimal exactly when \(v(\pi)\le1\); otherwise a maximizer supplies a negative-reduced-cost column.

notation.meaning: Maximum dual value of a feasible pattern

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given restricted-master prices \(\pi\), solve the pricing problem
\[
v(\pi)=\max_{p\in P}(a^p)^{\mathsf T}\pi.
\]
If \(v(\pi)>1\), any maximizing pattern has reduced cost \(1-v(\pi)<0\) and may be added to the master. If \(v(\pi)\le1\), then \((a^p)^{\mathsf T}\pi\le1\) for every full-master column, so \(\pi\) is full-dual feasible and the restricted-master optimum equals the full-master LP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing either returns a pattern valued above one, hence an improving column, or certifies full-master LP optimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An arc-flow master minimizes \(z\) subject to
\[
\sum_{e\in\delta^+(v)}f_e-\sum_{e\in\delta^-(v)}f_e=
\begin{cases}z,&v=s,\\-z,&v=t,\\0,&v\in V\setminus\{s,t\},\end{cases}
\quad
\sum_{e\in E_i}f_e\ge d_i,
\quad f_e,z\in\mathbb Z_+.
\]
Because \(G\) is acyclic, every integral \(s\)-\(t\) flow decomposes into \(z\) path flows. Under the path-pattern correspondence, this decomposition is exactly a multiset of feasible cutting patterns covering the demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer source-sink flow represents stock objects; path decomposition turns each unit of flow into one feasible cutting pattern.

children.title: Pattern-Preserving Graph Compression Calculus
children.top_down_role: State aggregation preserving feasible pattern coverage.

children.title: State Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Aggregation of network states representing equivalent partial patterns.

assumptions_latex: The labeled state graph is a directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\).
Each source-sink path encodes its sequence or count vector of item labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid aggregation preserves exactly the feasible source-sink pattern labels after quotienting states.

notation.meaning: Set of labels of source-sink paths

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic definition of aggregation suitable for pattern-preserving arc-flow compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A state aggregation is an equivalence relation \(\sim\) on \(V\) whose quotient graph \(G/\!\sim\) replaces each state by its equivalence class and maps every labeled arc \((u,v)\) to the correspondingly labeled class arc \(([u],[v])\). The aggregation is pattern-preserving when
\[
\mathcal L(G/\!\sim)=\mathcal L(G),
\]
where \(\mathcal L\) records complete source-sink path labels, including multiplicity when distinct paths represent distinct pattern variables. This equality excludes aggregations that create spurious feasible patterns or delete existing ones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State aggregation merges equivalent graph states; it is valid only when the quotient preserves exactly all source-sink pattern labels.
knowledge_statements.title: State Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a plausible semantic criterion for pattern-preserving state aggregation, but quotient graphs can create new concatenated paths, so the equality criterion and multiplicity convention require an arc-flow compression source.

children.title: Graph Compression
children.top_down_role: Reduction of arc-flow network size while retaining relevant paths.

assumptions_latex: The input is a finite labeled acyclic source-sink graph \(G\).
A certified pattern-preserving state equivalence \(\sim\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output graph is smaller or equal in size and has the same represented pattern family as \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient-and-prune compression with an externally validated state equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(G\) and \(\sim\), first form the labeled quotient \(G/\!\sim\), coalescing parallel arcs only when their labels and pattern multiplicity semantics agree. Next delete every state and arc lying on no source-sink path. Return the resulting graph \(G'\). Stop when no further certified equivalence classes or unreachable elements remain. Since every transformation is required to preserve complete path labels,
\[
\mathcal L(G')=\mathcal L(G),
\]
and \(G'\) can replace \(G\) in the associated arc-flow master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merge certified equivalent states, carefully coalesce compatible arcs, and remove elements outside all source-sink paths while preserving represented patterns.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quotient-and-prune procedure fits the Graph Compression algorithm container, but its preservation guarantee depends entirely on the externally certified equivalence and delicate parallel-arc semantics. No source supports those conditions or the stated stopping rule.

children.title: Pattern-Preserving Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between compressed paths and feasible cutting patterns.

assumptions_latex: Each labeled source-sink path represents one pattern column.
Path multiplicities are retained when they distinguish master variables or coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two graphs are pattern-preserving equivalent exactly when their complete path-to-pattern multisets coincide.

notation.meaning: Pattern multiset represented by graph G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence criterion for original and compressed arc-flow graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For labeled source-sink graphs \(G_1\) and \(G_2\), define
\[
G_1\equiv_P G_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathcal P(G_1)=\mathcal P(G_2),
\]
where \(\mathcal P(G)\) is the multiset of pattern columns induced by complete source-sink paths of \(G\). Hence equivalence requires both directions: every path pattern of \(G_1\) occurs in \(G_2\), and every path pattern of \(G_2\) occurs in \(G_1\), with relevant multiplicities preserved. Under this condition, both graphs generate the same pattern master after path-flow decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two arc-flow graphs are pattern-preserving equivalent when their source-sink paths induce exactly the same pattern columns, including relevant multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Preserving Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bidirectional equality criterion fits the equivalence container, but treating path-induced pattern columns as a multiset is representation-dependent and requires a source clarifying when duplicate paths constitute distinct master variables.

children.title: Initial Pattern Bases
children.top_down_role: Feasible starting pattern families for the restricted master.

assumptions_latex: Stock length is \(L>0\), and every item length satisfies \(0<\ell_i\le L\).
Demands satisfy \(d_i\in\mathbb Z_+\).
The restricted master uses covering demand rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed homogeneous-pattern basis is feasible for the covering restricted master.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of type-i items fitting in one stock object
Homogeneous pattern for item type i
Initial multiplicity of homogeneous pattern i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive feasible initialization for a one-dimensional covering restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each item type \(i\), compute \(q_i=\lfloor L/\ell_i\rfloor\ge1\) and insert the homogeneous feasible pattern \(a^{(i)}=q_i e_i\) into the restricted master. Initialize its multiplicity by
\[
x_i^0=\left\lceil\frac{d_i}{q_i}\right\rceil.
\]
Then \(q_i x_i^0\ge d_i\) for every \(i\), so the initial restricted covering master is feasible. The algorithm outputs the pattern family \(\{a^{(i)}:d_i>0\}\) and the feasible starting vector \(x^0\); zero-demand types need no initial column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with one maximal homogeneous pattern per demanded item type; suitable multiplicities immediately yield a feasible covering restricted master.
knowledge_statements.title: Initial Pattern Bases

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogeneous-pattern initialization is mathematically valid for the stated one-dimensional covering master and the algorithm kind fits the container, but no source is provided.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Wide-first construction of an initial cutting-pattern basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization heuristic for cutting-stock revised simplex with delayed column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume one raw width \(r\), demands \(b_i\ge0\), and \(r\ge w_1>w_2>\cdots>w_m>0\). Initialize \(R=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(b_i'=b_i\). At iteration \(j\), set \(a_i=0\) for \(i\notin R\) and recursively set \(a_i=\left\lfloor(r-\sum_{k<i}w_k a_k)/w_i\right\rfloor\) for \(i\in R\). Let \(x_j=\min\{b_i'/a_i:i\in R,\ a_i>0\}\), remove an index \(k\) attaining the minimum, and update each remaining residual demand by \(b_i'\leftarrow b_i'-x_j a_i\). Repeating for \(m\) iterations constructs feasible patterns and a demand-satisfying initial solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order final widths from widest to narrowest. Each iteration greedily constructs a pattern from the remaining item types, uses it until at least one residual demand becomes zero, removes such a demand, and updates the others. One demand is eliminated per iteration.
assumptions_latex: r\ge w_1>w_2>\cdots>w_m>0
b_i\ge0
R_1=\{1,\ldots,m\},\quad b_i'=b_i
\{i\in R:a_i>0\}\ne\varnothing\text{ at every iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{After }m\text{ iterations, the constructed feasible pattern matrix }B\text{ and }x\ge0\text{ satisfy }Bx=b.

children.title: Active Pattern Pools
children.top_down_role: Collections of generated patterns maintained for restricted-master use.

assumptions_latex: A one-dimensional cutting-stock master problem has item demands \(b\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), pattern set \(\mathcal P\), and pattern vectors \(a^p\in\mathbb{Z}_+^m\).
Column generation is at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted master at iteration \(k\) is formed from exactly the columns indexed by \(P_k\).

notation.meaning: set of all feasible cutting patterns
active pattern pool at iteration k
restricted-master variable associated with pattern p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restricted masters are indexed by a finite current subset of feasible columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite pool currently admitted to the restricted cutting-stock master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An active pattern pool at iteration \(k\) is a finite subset \(P_k\subseteq\mathcal P\). Its restricted master is
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P_k}c_p x_p:\sum_{p\in P_k}a^p x_p\ge b,\ x_p\ge0\text{ for every }p\in P_k\right\}.
\]
A newly priced pattern may enter \(P_k\), while an inactive pattern may be stored outside it. Thus membership in \(P_k\), rather than prior generation alone, determines whether the variable \(x_p\) and its column \(a^p\) occur in the current restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active pool is the finite set of generated patterns whose variables and coefficients currently appear in the restricted cutting-stock master.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Pattern Pools

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable source is cited. The coefficient c_p is not introduced, and the plain statement restricts the pool to generated patterns whereas the formal definition only requires a finite feasible-pattern subset.

children.title: Column Retention Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for retaining useful generated columns.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), a finite active pool \(P_k\) and a set \(G_k\) of newly generated improving patterns are available.
Each active pattern has recorded master activity, reduced-cost history, and age.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pattern required by the stated safeguards remains in \(P_{k+1}\).

notation.meaning: active pattern pool at iteration k
newly generated patterns at iteration k
retained subset selected from the old pool

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: practical restricted-master management retains protected and recently useful columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A safeguarded policy template, not a claim that one threshold choice is universally best.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an incumbent restricted-master solution \(x^k\), reduced costs \(\bar c_p^k\), ages \(h_p^k\), thresholds \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_c\ge0\), and age limit \(H\), form
\[
R_k=\{p\in P_k:x_p^k>\varepsilon_x\ \text{or}\ \bar c_p^k<\varepsilon_c\ \text{or}\ h_p^k\le H\}\cup F_k,
\]
where \(F_k\subseteq P_k\) contains columns protected for feasibility or an incumbent solution. Set \(P_{k+1}=R_k\cup G_k\), remove duplicates, and reset the age of generated or active columns. Stop management after this update and return \(P_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain protected, active, recently useful, or young columns; unite them with newly generated patterns and remove duplicates to obtain the next active pool.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Retention Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the policy leaf, but the retention tests, safeguards, and age-reset rule are implementation-specific and have no cited support. The instruction to reset the age of generated or active columns is also ambiguous.

children.title: Column Removal Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for retiring inactive or redundant columns.

assumptions_latex: The current restricted master is feasible and has active pool \(P_k\).
A protected set \(F_k\subseteq P_k\) is sufficient to preserve designated feasibility or incumbent information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated pool is \(P_{k+1}=P_k\setminus D_k\), and no protected column is deleted.

notation.meaning: protected columns that cannot be removed at iteration k
number of consecutive inactive iterations for pattern p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stale nonbasic columns may be removed while feasibility-critical columns are protected
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes safeguarded deletion from a restricted master without asserting convergence for arbitrary thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose tolerances \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_c\ge0\) and an inactivity limit \(H\). Define eligible deletions by
\[
E_k=\{p\in P_k\setminus F_k:x_p^k\le\varepsilon_x,\ \bar c_p^k\ge-\varepsilon_c,\ h_p^k>H\}.
\]
Select any \(D_k\subseteq E_k\) satisfying the prescribed pool-size limit. Before deletion, verify that the master restricted to \(P_k\setminus D_k\) retains every required protected column and remains feasible; otherwise shrink \(D_k\) until it does. Return \(P_{k+1}=P_k\setminus D_k\) and archive the removed patterns for possible regeneration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only stale, nonprotected, nonimproving columns, and reduce the deletion set whenever its removal would violate the required restricted-master safeguards.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Removal Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the removal-policy leaf and its safeguards are coherent, but the deletion criteria and claimed lifecycle practice lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Pattern Reuse Across Masters
children.top_down_role: Reuse of previously generated patterns across related restricted masters.

assumptions_latex: Two restricted masters use the same item types and stock capacity, or admit an explicit item-index mapping.
A stored pattern satisfies the target master's physical packing constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted stored pattern is a valid target-master column, although it need not have negative reduced cost under the target dual vector.

notation.meaning: mapping from source to target item coordinates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a column can be transferred only when its coefficients satisfy the target subproblem constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States validity conditions for warm-starting a compatible master with previously generated patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let source pattern \(a\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) be mapped to target coordinates by \(T\). It is reusable in the target master precisely when
\[
Ta\in\mathbb Z_+^{m'},\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{m'}w_i'(Ta)_i\le L',
\]
and its target column coefficients equal the target constraints' contributions for \(Ta\). If target restrictions include bounds or incompatibilities, \(Ta\) must satisfy them as well. Reuse authorizes insertion into the target pool; it does not certify improvement, which must be checked using the target costs and current target dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored pattern may seed another master only after coordinate mapping and validation against every target packing constraint; target reduced cost must be recomputed.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Reuse Across Masters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but cross-master equivalence and the sufficiency of the coordinate mapping are model-dependent. No source supports the stated necessary-and-sufficient reuse condition.

children.title: Knapsack Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pattern generation through a knapsack-structured auxiliary problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the cutting-stock column-pricing problem as an unbounded integer knapsack formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(W\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), widths \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) with \(w_i\le W\), and pricing coefficients \(p_i\in\mathbb R\), a pattern maximizing \(p^\top a\) is obtained by solving \[\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m p_i a_i:\ \sum_{i=1}^m w_i a_i\le W,\ a_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\right\}.\] This is an unbounded integer knapsack problem, where “unbounded” refers to the absence of individual upper bounds on the item multiplicities apart from the capacity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing a cutting-stock column means selecting nonnegative integer multiplicities of the requested widths, subject to the stock-width capacity, to maximize their total pricing value. This is an unbounded integer knapsack problem.
assumptions_latex: W\in\mathbb Z_{>0}
w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\quad w_i\le W\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
p\in\mathbb R^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\left\{p^\top a:\ w^\top a\le W,\ a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m\right\}\quad\text{is the cutting-stock pattern-pricing problem and has unbounded-integer-knapsack form.}

source_evidence.locator: Large scale optimization / 6.2. The cutting stock problem / Definition 6.2-extra-2

source_refs.locator: Large scale optimization / 6.2. The cutting stock problem / Definition 6.2-extra-2

knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack pricing for cutting-stock patterns

source_witnesses.locator: Large scale optimization / 6.2. The cutting stock problem / Definition 6.2-extra-2

children.title: Exact Pricing Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Pricing families supporting complete LP optimality certification.

children.title: Exact Knapsack Pricing
children.top_down_role: Complete solution of the pricing subproblem for candidate patterns.

assumptions_latex: Item widths \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), stock length \(L\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and dual prices \(\pi_i\in\mathbb R\) are given.
Every feasible pattern is a nonnegative integer vector satisfying the stock-capacity constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pattern minimizes reduced cost over the complete feasible pattern set and therefore exactly resolves the pricing question.

notation.meaning: optimal dual value captured by one pattern
reduced cost of pattern a for unit roll cost

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Gilmore-Gomory pricing for one-dimensional cutting stock is an unbounded integer knapsack problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses unit stock cost and the unbounded integer-knapsack form of cutting-stock pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\mathcal P=\left\{a\in\mathbb Z_+^m:\sum_{i=1}^m w_i a_i\le L\right\},\qquad z^*(\pi)=\max_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{i=1}^m\pi_i a_i.
\]
Solve this integer knapsack problem to global optimality and return an optimizer \(a^*\). Its reduced cost is \(\bar c(a^*)=1-z^*(\pi)\). If \(z^*(\pi)>1\), output \(a^*\) as an improving column. If \(z^*(\pi)\le1\), output the exact optimum value and optimizer as the pricing result, certifying that no feasible pattern has negative reduced cost under \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the unbounded integer knapsack globally. Its optimizer is the most negative-reduced-cost pattern, or its optimum proves that no improving pattern exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Knapsack Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly represents unit-cost one-dimensional cutting-stock pricing as an unbounded integer knapsack, but no authoritative cutting-stock locator is supplied. The usual nonnegative domain of covering-master dual prices is also unstated.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Optimality Certification
children.top_down_role: Certification based on the absence of improving pattern values.

assumptions_latex: The restricted cutting-stock master is feasible and solved to optimality with dual vector \(\pi\).
The pricing maximum is evaluated over every feasible pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(z^*(\pi)\le1\), the restricted-master primal solution is optimal for the full master linear relaxation.

notation.meaning: maximum dual value of any feasible pattern

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact nonnegative reduced costs plus restricted-master strong duality certify full-master LP optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies optimality of the full master LP, not integrality or optimality of the integer cutting-stock model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^R\) and \(\pi\ge0\) be optimal primal and dual solutions of the restricted master, and compute
\[
z^*(\pi)=\max_{a\in\mathcal P}\pi^\top a.
\]
For unit pattern cost, the certificate predicate is \(z^*(\pi)\le1\), equivalently \(1-\pi^\top a\ge0\) for every \(a\in\mathcal P\). Restricted-master strong duality gives \(\mathbf1^\top x^R=b^\top\pi\); full dual feasibility then makes \(b^\top\pi\) a lower bound on every full-master primal solution. Hence equality certifies that \(x^R\), extended by zeros on absent columns, is full-master LP-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal restricted master plus exact proof that every feasible pattern has nonnegative reduced cost certifies optimality for the full master linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Optimality Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and LP-only scope are appropriate, but b and the full pattern set are not introduced within the record, and the standard covering-master formulation needed for the displayed strong-duality equality is not stated or cited.

children.title: Pricing Completeness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which a pricing procedure does not support complete certification.

assumptions_latex: A pricing procedure searches a subset \(Q\subseteq\mathcal P\) of feasible patterns.
The current dual vector is \(\pi\), and pattern cost is one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure to find improvement in \(Q\) certifies full pricing optimality exactly when an independently valid bound proves \(\max_{a\in\mathcal P}\pi^\top a\le1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restricted pricing search cannot exclude improving columns outside its search domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates discovery over a restricted search set from complete reduced-cost certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Searching only \(Q\subsetneq\mathcal P\) and obtaining
\[
\max_{a\in Q}\pi^\top a\le1
\]
does not imply \(\max_{a\in\mathcal P}\pi^\top a\le1\). The inference is valid only if \(Q=\mathcal P\), or if a valid global upper bound \(U\) satisfies \(\pi^\top a\le U\le1\) for all \(a\in\mathcal P\setminus Q\). Indeed, whenever some unsearched \(a'\in\mathcal P\setminus Q\) has \(\pi^\top a'>1\), its reduced cost \(1-\pi^\top a'\) is negative although restricted pricing reports no improving column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No improvement in a restricted search is not a global certificate unless all patterns were covered or a valid bound excludes improvement among unsearched patterns.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Completeness Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is correct and the restricted-versus-complete pricing distinction is mathematically sound, but no inspectable column-generation source is provided.

children.title: Heuristic Pricing
children.top_down_role: Fast discovery of improving patterns before exact certification.

assumptions_latex: A current dual vector \(\pi\) and a finite-time knapsack heuristic \(H\) are available.
Every pattern returned by \(H\) is checked for feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted output is a valid improving column, while an empty output carries no full-master optimality implication.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: heuristic pricing may discover improving columns but cannot certify their absence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fast pattern discovery followed by exact feasibility and reduced-cost checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\pi\), run \(H(\pi)\) to produce a finite candidate set \(C\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^m\). Discard every \(a\in C\) violating \(\sum_i w_i a_i\le L\), and compute \(\bar c(a)=1-\pi^\top a\) for each remaining candidate. Return one or more candidates satisfying \(\bar c(a)<-\varepsilon\), ordered by reduced cost or another declared score. If none passes the test, return \(\varnothing\) and invoke exact pricing before making a full-master optimality claim; heuristic failure alone is not a stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate candidate patterns quickly, validate them exactly, and return those with sufficiently negative reduced cost. Failure requires exact pricing before termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its noncertification warning fit heuristic pricing, but m, the item widths, stock length, and the tolerance epsilon are not introduced in the assumptions or notation. No authoritative source is cited.

children.title: Diversified Multi-Column Pricing Family
children.top_down_role: Generation of several useful patterns per pricing round.

children.title: Multi-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Generation of several improving patterns within one pricing round.

assumptions_latex: The current dual vector \(\pi\), feasible pattern set \(\mathcal P\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and batch limit \(K\ge1\) are given.
Candidate reduced costs can be evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output contains at most \(K\) distinct feasible columns, each having reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multi-column pricing inserts a batch of distinct negative-reduced-cost columns per iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies batch generation without requiring a particular diversification score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form or search the improving set
\[
I(\pi)=\{a\in\mathcal P:1-\pi^\top a<-\varepsilon\}.
\]
Initialize \(B=\varnothing\). Repeatedly select a pattern \(a\in I(\pi)\setminus B\) according to a declared ranking rule, add it to \(B\), and optionally impose an exclusion rule before the next selection. Stop when \(|B|=K\), no eligible improving pattern remains, or the pricing time limit is reached. Return all patterns in \(B\) simultaneously to the restricted master. A nonexhaustive empty batch does not certify pricing optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing returns a batch of at most K distinct negative-reduced-cost patterns, stopping at the batch limit, exhaustion, or a declared resource limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Column Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits multi-column pricing, but the mechanism for forming or searching the improving set and the meaning of exhaustion under optional exclusions are underspecified. No source supports the proposed template.

children.title: Diversified Pattern Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of structurally varied patterns for master enrichment.

assumptions_latex: A finite candidate set \(C\) of feasible improving patterns and a batch limit \(K\) are given.
A nonnegative dissimilarity \(d(a,a')\) and relevance score \(s(a)\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned batch contains at most \(K\) candidates and satisfies the declared relevance-diversity selection rule.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diversified batch selection trades reduced-cost relevance against pattern dissimilarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit threshold-based diversification rule for a finite improving candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(B=\varnothing\). While \(|B|<K\), define
\[
E(B)=\{a\in C\setminus B:d(a,a')\ge\delta\text{ for every }a'\in B\}.
\]
If \(E(B)=\varnothing\), stop. Otherwise choose \(a^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in E(B)}s(a)\), add \(a^*\) to \(B\), and repeat. Return \(B\). With \(s(a)=-\bar c(a)\), the construction prioritizes reduced-cost improvement subject to pairwise separation \(d(a,a')\ge\delta\); the choices of \(d\) and \(\delta\) are part of the policy specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily choose high-scoring improving patterns while enforcing a minimum pairwise dissimilarity, until the batch is full or no eligible candidate remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Diversified Pattern Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The greedy algorithm fits the selection leaf, but delta is not introduced among the assumptions and the particular threshold-based diversity policy has no cited support.

children.title: Duplicate-Column Control
children.top_down_role: Management of repeated or near-duplicate generated patterns.

assumptions_latex: Pattern vectors use a fixed canonical item ordering.
A current pool \(P_k\) and a generated candidate list \(C_k\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned insertion set contains exactly one representative of each new canonical pattern class and no class already represented in \(P_k\).

notation.meaning: canonical encoding of a pattern vector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical hashing prevents repeated insertion of identical master columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controls exact duplicates under a declared canonical pattern encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the occupied-key set \(S=\{\kappa(a):a\in P_k\}\) and initialize \(B_k=\varnothing\). Process candidates \(a\in C_k\) in declared priority order. If \(\kappa(a)\in S\), reject \(a\); otherwise add \(a\) to \(B_k\) and add \(\kappa(a)\) to \(S\). Return \(B_k\) for insertion. The encoding must satisfy \(\kappa(a)=\kappa(a')\) whenever \(a\) and \(a'\) induce the same declared pattern representation; stronger equivalence, such as identical master columns from different patterns, requires a correspondingly stronger canonical key.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize each pattern, reject keys already present or accepted in the same batch, and insert one representative of every genuinely new pattern class.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Column Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits duplicate control, but the one-way condition imposed on the canonical encoding does not fully characterize when two keys represent the same declared class. The model-dependent equivalence rule also lacks a source.

children.title: Column-Generation Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Families addressing dual oscillation, degeneracy, and tailing-off.

children.title: Dual Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Control of unstable dual pattern valuations.

assumptions_latex: A current restricted-master dual vector \(\pi^k\), stabilization center \(\hat\pi^k\), and parameter \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) are given.
Pricing is ultimately solved exactly using a dual vector for which valid reduced costs are computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized vector tempers dual movement for pricing, while exact termination must still be certified against a valid current dual solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex-combination dual stabilization dampens pricing-vector oscillation but requires valid terminal certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A convex-combination stabilization template with an explicit exact-certification safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute
\[
\tilde\pi^k=(1-\alpha_k)\hat\pi^k+\alpha_k\pi^k.
\]
Use \(\tilde\pi^k\) to search for promising patterns and add every pattern whose reduced cost is confirmed under the dual vector required by the master algorithm. Update the center by a declared rule, for example \(\hat\pi^{k+1}=\tilde\pi^k\) after serious progress, and otherwise retain \(\hat\pi^k\). Before termination, solve pricing exactly at a valid optimal restricted-master dual vector \(\pi^k\); absence of improvement only at \(\tilde\pi^k\) is not by itself an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend the current dual solution with a stabilization center for pricing, update the center after progress, and use exact unstabilized pricing for final certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Stabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a plausible dual-stabilization template, but the center update, convergence safeguards, and dual vector used to confirm intermediate reduced costs are method-dependent or ambiguous. No authoritative stabilization source is cited.

children.title: Dual-Restriction Strengthening Calculus
children.top_down_role: Additional dual structure used to accelerate convergence.

children.title: Valid Dual Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Additional valid structure imposed in dual space.

knowledge_statements.title: Valid Dual Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality-preserving inequalities for the dual of a cutting-stock master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{\pi\in\mathbb R_+^m:A^{\mathsf T}\pi\le \mathbf 1\}\), let \(v^*=\max\{d^{\mathsf T}\pi:\pi\in D\}\), and let \(D^*=\{\pi\in D:d^{\mathsf T}\pi=v^*\}\). A system \(H\pi\le h\) is a valid dual-inequality system, in the dual-optimal sense, precisely when \[D^*\cap\{\pi:H\pi\le h\}\ne\varnothing.\] Thus the inequalities may exclude dual-feasible points, but they must retain at least one full-master dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual inequalities are valid for stabilization when imposing them preserves at least one optimal solution of the full master dual.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(A\) is the complete pattern matrix.
The full master dual has a finite attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*\cap\{\pi:H\pi\le h\}\ne\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports this dual-optimal notion of validity.

children.title: Dual-Bound Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Tighter dual bounds used to improve restricted-master progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of optimality-preserving restrictions on a restricted-master dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted pattern set \(P_R\subseteq P\), define \(D_R=\{\pi\ge0:A_R^{\mathsf T}\pi\le\mathbf1\}\) and \(z_R=\max_{\pi\in D_R}d^{\mathsf T}\pi\). If \(H\pi\le h\) is valid in the sense that it contains some full-master dual optimum, then \(z_R^H=\max\{d^{\mathsf T}\pi:\pi\in D_R,\ H\pi\le h\}\) satisfies \[z^*\le z_R^H\le z_R.\] Hence the restriction strengthens the restricted-master upper bound for the minimization master without invalidating it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimality-preserving dual restriction can only lower the restricted-master bound, while keeping it no smaller than the full-master optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(P_R\subseteq P\).
Strong duality holds for the full and restricted master LPs.
Some \(\pi^*\in D^*\) satisfies \(H\pi^*\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*\le z_R^H\le z_R\).

notation.meaning: Restricted-master dual optimum after imposing the dual restrictions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound ordering is coherent under the stated assumptions and the property kind fits, but the record has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Pricing-Compatible Dual Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Dual restrictions whose effects remain manageable in pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Dual Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle compatibility of stabilization restrictions with cutting-stock pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\{\pi:H\pi\le h\}\) be a dual restriction and let \(P\) be the implicit pattern set. The restriction is pricing-compatible when membership in \(H\) is decidable without enumerating \(P\), and the usual pricing oracle still computes \[\rho(\pi)=\min_{p\in P}\bigl(1-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr)\] for every restricted dual vector \(\pi\in H\). Exact pricing then either returns a pattern with \(\rho(\pi)<0\) or certifies \(a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\le1\) for every \(p\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual restriction is pricing-compatible when it is explicitly testable and leaves exact pattern separation implementable by the usual pricing oracle.
assumptions_latex: Every pattern has unit master cost.
The pattern-pricing oracle optimizes over the complete set \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\pi)\ge0\iff a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\le1\ \text{for all }p\in P\).

notation.meaning: Complete set of feasible cutting patterns.
Minimum reduced cost returned by pricing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the proposed meaning of pricing compatibility is not demonstrably standard and lacks evidence. The symbol H is also used both for a restriction set and as the matrix in Hπ≤h.

children.title: Terminal Convergence Control Regimes
children.top_down_role: Master and pricing mechanisms for slow terminal convergence.

children.title: Master Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Restricted-master behavior with many equivalent or weakly distinguished solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy of a restricted cutting-stock master basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write a restricted master in equality standard form as \(B x_B+N x_N=d\), with \(x_B,x_N\ge0\) and nonsingular basis matrix \(B\). The associated basic feasible solution is degenerate when \[x_B=B^{-1}d\quad\text{and}\quad (x_B)_j=0\ \text{for at least one basic index }j.\] Equivalently, fewer than \(m\) basic variables are strictly positive in an \(m\)-row nonredundant master. Degeneracy permits a pivot or column insertion with zero primal step and no immediate objective improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-master basis is degenerate when at least one basic variable equals zero, allowing basis changes without a positive primal step.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is represented in equality standard form.
Its \(m\) rows are nonredundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists j\in B\text{ such that }(B^{-1}d)_j=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The core definition is standard and fits the leaf, but no source is cited. The conclusion writes j∈B although B was introduced as a matrix, and the claimed pivot or insertion consequence requires more precise qualifications.

children.title: Terminal Tailing-Off
children.top_down_role: Slow progress near completion of the column-generation process.

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Tailing-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotically negligible progress near column-generation termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k\) be the nonincreasing restricted-master objective values for a minimization master, with \(z_k\downarrow z^*>0\). Terminal tailing-off occurs when infinitely many iterations remain nonterminal while \[\frac{z_k-z_{k+1}}{z_k-z^*}\longrightarrow0.\] Thus each late column or basis change removes a vanishing fraction of the remaining master gap. Degenerate zero-step pivots are an extreme case, since \(z_{k+1}=z_k\) although the pricing or basis state changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing-off occurs when late iterations close a vanishing fraction of the remaining master gap, potentially including zero-improvement degenerate pivots.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\) converges monotonically to a positive full-master optimum \(z^*\).
The algorithm has not yet produced an exact termination certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the displayed asymptotic ratio is a specialized formalization rather than an established definition supported by the supplied inventory. An authoritative source is required before accepting it.

children.title: Anti-Degeneracy Control
children.top_down_role: Master-side mechanisms addressing degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Anti-Degeneracy Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal selection of stable dual solutions on degenerate optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted dual feasible set \(D_R\), a reference vector \(\bar\pi_k\), and \(\mu_k>0\), compute \[\pi_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi\in D_R}\left\{d^{\mathsf T}\pi-\frac{\mu_k}{2}\lVert\pi-\bar\pi_k\rVert_2^2\right\}.\] Price exactly at \(\pi_k\); add a negative-reduced-cost pattern when one exists, and update \(\bar\pi_{k+1}\) to an accepted dual center. Decrease \(\mu_k\) toward zero. Terminate only when exact pricing finds no negative reduced cost for an unstabilized dual-optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a proximal dual point, price there, update the center, and remove stabilization before accepting exact termination.
assumptions_latex: Each stabilized restricted-dual problem is solved exactly.
Final certification uses an unstabilized restricted-master optimum and exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\pi_k)\ge0\) at an unstabilized dual optimum is the stopping condition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a plausible proximal column-generation algorithm, but no source supports the update schedule or termination safeguard. Evidence is also needed that proximal dual stabilization belongs in this exact anti-degeneracy leaf rather than only a broader stabilization container.

children.title: Late-Stage Pricing Control
children.top_down_role: Pricing policies aimed at slow terminal progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Late-Stage Pricing Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive transition from heuristic to exact pricing near termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master and obtain dual vector \(\pi_k\). While a heuristic pricing oracle returns a pattern \(p\) with \(1-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_k<0\), add such patterns. If the heuristic fails, the bound gap is below a prescribed threshold, or progress stalls, invoke exact pricing to compute \[\rho_k=\min_{p\in P}\bigl(1-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_k\bigr).\] Add an exact minimizer when \(\rho_k<0\); otherwise stop. Heuristic failure alone is never a termination condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use heuristic pricing for speed, switch to exact pricing after failure or near convergence, and terminate only on an exact nonnegative reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: The exact pricing oracle optimizes over every feasible pattern.
Each restricted master is solved to the accuracy required by its pricing test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{terminate}\iff\rho_k\ge0\text{ under exact pricing}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and exact-pricing termination safeguard fit the leaf, but the switching policy and stopping claim have no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Column-Generation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates connecting pricing status, master bounds, and LP optimality.

children.title: No-Improving-Pattern Certificate
children.top_down_role: Termination certification supplied by exact pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: No-Improving-Pattern Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-pricing certificate for full-master dual feasibility and LP termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\ge0\) be optimal for the current restricted-master dual, and let exact pricing return \[\rho(\pi)=\min_{p\in P}\bigl(1-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr).\] If \(\rho(\pi)\ge0\), then \(a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\le1\) for every feasible pattern \(p\), so \(\pi\) is feasible for the full-master dual. Because the restricted primal solution is full-master feasible and has objective \(d^{\mathsf T}\pi\), both solutions are optimal for their respective full master LPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative exact minimum reduced cost proves full dual feasibility; matching restricted primal and dual values then certify full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is solved optimally.
Pricing is exact over the complete pattern set \(P\).
Restricted-master columns are feasible full-master patterns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\pi)\ge0\Longrightarrow z_R=z^* = d^{\mathsf T}\pi\).

notation.meaning: Exact minimum reduced cost over all patterns.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically coherent and matches the terminal container, but no cited column-generation source with a specific locator supports it.

children.title: Master-Bound Transfer Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Bound information coordinating restricted and full master problems.

children.title: Restricted-Master Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bound information derived from the current restricted column set.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual bounds furnished by a restricted pattern set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_R\subseteq P\), let \(z_R\) be the optimum of the restricted covering master and \(z^*\) the full-master optimum. Restricting a minimization master to fewer columns gives \[z^*\le z_R.\] By restricted-master strong duality, \(z_R=d^{\mathsf T}\pi_R\) for an optimal restricted dual vector \(\pi_R\). This equality does not make \(d^{\mathsf T}\pi_R\) a full-master lower bound unless \(\pi_R\) also satisfies every omitted pattern inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted primal optimum is an upper bound on the full optimum; its dual value becomes a full lower bound only after all omitted constraints are certified.
assumptions_latex: \(P_R\subseteq P\).
The restricted master is feasible and has a finite optimum.
Strong duality holds for the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*\le z_R=d^{\mathsf T}\pi_R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly distinguishes the restricted-primal upper bound from full-dual feasibility, but it lacks a supporting source and locator.

children.title: Full-Master Bound Transfer
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of restricted-master information for the full pattern model.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Master Bound Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of restricted-dual values using exact or bounded-error pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi_R\ge0\) be optimal for the restricted dual and suppose exact pricing certifies \(1-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_R\ge-\varepsilon\) for all \(p\in P\), where \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Then \(a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_R\le1+\varepsilon\), so \(\widehat\pi=\pi_R/(1+\varepsilon)\) is full-dual feasible. Consequently, \[\frac{d^{\mathsf T}\pi_R}{1+\varepsilon}\le z^*\le z_R.\] For \(\varepsilon=0\), the restricted-dual value transfers unchanged and equals the full-master optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified reduced-cost error permits scaling the restricted dual into a full-feasible dual, yielding a rigorous lower bound and exact transfer at zero error.
assumptions_latex: Every master column has unit cost.
Pricing covers the complete pattern set.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) is a certified uniform reduced-cost tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}\pi_R/(1+\varepsilon)\le z^*\le z_R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaling argument is coherent for nonnegative dual variables and unit column costs, and certificate is an appropriate kind. The approximate-pricing bound transfer nevertheless has no cited evidence.

children.title: Global Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates coordinating master bounds with complete pricing information.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual equality certificate for the full cutting-stock master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x,\pi)\) is a global LP-optimality certificate when \(x\ge0\), \(Ax\ge d\), \(\pi\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\pi\le\mathbf1\), and \[\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=d^{\mathsf T}\pi.\] The primal and dual feasibility checks establish opposite weak-duality bounds, while equality closes the gap. In column generation, full dual feasibility is verifiable through an exact no-improving-pattern certificate rather than explicit enumeration of all columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full primal feasibility, full dual feasibility, and equal objectives form a verifiable global optimality certificate for the master LP.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) contains every feasible cutting pattern.
The primal and dual master LPs use the displayed covering formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=d^{\mathsf T}\pi=z^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-dual equality certificate is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no authoritative textbook section, theorem, or page is cited.

children.title: Cutting-Stock Integer Solution Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods converting fractional pattern solutions into certified integer cutting plans.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Exact Solution of Cutting Stock Problems Using Column Generation and Branch-and-Bound

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: An Exact Algorithm for IP Column Generation
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: An Exact Algorithm for IP Column Generation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative LP-relaxation scheme for an integer program. The extract gives no finite-termination guarantee and presupposes optimal solution of each relaxation and generation of a separating valid inequality whenever its optimum is fractional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an integer program \(\mathrm{IP}\) and its LP relaxation \(\mathrm{LP}\), repeatedly solve \(\mathrm{LP}\) and let \(x^*\) be an optimal solution. If \(x^*\) is integral, return it. Otherwise, append a linear inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) that every integer-feasible solution satisfies but \(x^*\) violates, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the LP relaxation. An integral relaxation optimum is optimal for the integer program; otherwise, add an inequality valid for every integer-feasible solution but violated by the current fractional optimum, and resolve.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm{LP}\) is a relaxation of \(\mathrm{IP}\) with the same objective.
The current relaxation has an optimal solution \(x^*\).
Whenever \(x^*\) is nonintegral, an inequality valid for every integer-feasible solution and violated by \(x^*\) can be generated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\mathbb Z^n\Rightarrow x^*\text{ is optimal for }\mathrm{IP}\); otherwise the valid inequality is added and the relaxation is solved again.

source_evidence.locator: Integer programming methods / 11.1. Cutting plane methods / Algorithm 11.1-extra-2

children.title: Fractional-Solution Integer Recovery Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Integer construction from fractional pattern solutions.

children.title: Pattern Rounding-Fixing Calculus
children.top_down_role: Classical rounding and variable-fixing families.

children.title: Fractional Pattern Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding families applied to fractional pattern multiplicities.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Pattern Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floor-and-repair recovery of an integer cutting plan from a fractional master solution.
