knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible fractional pattern vector \(x^*\ge0\), set \(y_p=\lfloor x_p^*\rfloor\) for every generated pattern and compute residual demand \[r_i=\max\left\{0,d_i-\sum_p a_{ip}y_p\right\}.\] Solve or heuristically cover the residual instance to obtain \(w\in\mathbb Z_+^{P}\) satisfying \(Aw\ge r\). Return \(y+w\). If no residual cover is found, report failure rather than claiming feasibility. The returned solution uses \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(y+w)\) stock objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floor each fractional pattern count, compute uncovered demand, cover the residual instance, and combine both integer pattern vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is feasible for the fractional covering master.
All pattern coefficients and demands are nonnegative integers.
The repair phase returns an integer residual cover or reports failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(y+w)\ge d\quad\text{and}\quad y+w\in\mathbb Z_+^{P}.\)

notation.meaning: Componentwise floor of the fractional pattern vector.
Integer repair solution for the residual instance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The floor-and-repair algorithm is internally coherent and appropriately reports repair failure, but no cutting-stock source with a specific locator supports this recovery method.

children.title: Pattern Variable Fixing
children.top_down_role: Fixing policies for selected pattern variables.

assumptions_latex: The cutting-stock master is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge d,\ x\in\mathbb Z_+^{P}\}\).
A fractional master solution \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_+^P\), a fixing set \(F\subseteq P\), and integers \(k_p\ge0\) for \(p\in F\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the fixed partial solution and residual demand \(r\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixing selected master variables and updating uncovered demand is the standard residual construction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines fixing and residual updating, but leaves the heuristic choice of fixed variables local.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(F\) and \(k\), commonly with \(k_p\in\{\lfloor\bar x_p\rfloor,\lceil\bar x_p\rceil\}\), and impose \(x_p=k_p\) for every \(p\in F\). Compute
\[
r_i=\max\!\left\{0,d_i-\sum_{p\in F}a_{ip}k_p\right\}\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
The output is the partial integer vector \(x_F=k\), the remaining pattern set \(R=P\setminus F\), and residual demand \(r\). A fixing is accepted only if it respects all node restrictions and a prescribed residual-feasibility test; otherwise it is reversed or modified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix selected pattern counts to integers, subtract their production from demand, and retain the resulting nonnegative residual instance only when it passes a feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Variable Fixing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf and the residual-demand update is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports the stated floor-or-ceiling fixing convention or the unspecified residual-feasibility acceptance procedure. A cutting-stock heuristic source with a section or page locator is required.

children.title: Residual Feasibility After Fixing
children.top_down_role: Feasibility consequences left for the residual demand problem.

assumptions_latex: A partial fixing \(x_F=k\) has residual demand \(r=(d-A_Fk)_+\).
The remaining admissible pattern set is \(R=P\setminus F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual completion is feasible exactly when \(\exists y\in\mathbb Z_+^R\) with \(A_Ry\ge r\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility of a fixed partial covering solution is equivalent to integer coverability of its residual demand
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility condition for completing a partially fixed covering master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The fixing \(x_F=k\) is residually feasible if and only if
\[
\mathcal F(r,R)=\{y\in\mathbb Z_+^R:A_Ry\ge r\}\ne\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, there are nonnegative integer multiplicities of the unfixed admissible patterns whose aggregate item production dominates every component of \(r\). This condition concerns existence only; an LP-feasible residual master is necessary but, without an integrality property, is not sufficient for residual integer feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixing is residually feasible exactly when integer multiplicities of the remaining admissible patterns can cover every residual demand component.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Feasibility After Fixing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, and the integer-coverability condition is precise and consistent with the plain statement. However, the record has no citation supporting the residual-feasibility formulation or its LP-versus-integer qualification.

children.title: Residual-Demand Completion
children.top_down_role: Secondary optimization after partial integer construction.

assumptions_latex: A feasible partial integer pattern vector \(x_F=k\) and residual demand \(r=(d-A_Fk)_+\) are given.
A residual pattern family \(R\) and costs \(c_R\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the residual problem is feasible, \((k,y^*)\) is a complete feasible integer cutting plan.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual-demand completion is the secondary covering problem induced by a partial integer solution
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secondary integer covering optimization after fixing part of a cutting plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form the residual integer master
\[
y^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{c_R^{\mathsf T}y:A_Ry\ge r,\ y\in\mathbb Z_+^R\}.
\]
Solve it exactly or with a declared completion heuristic. If a feasible \(y^*\) is found, output \(x_p=k_p\) for \(p\in F\) and \(x_p=y_p^*\) for \(p\in R\); its cost is \(c_F^{\mathsf T}k+c_R^{\mathsf T}y^*\). If the residual master is infeasible, reject or revise the preceding fixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a secondary integer covering problem for the uncovered demand, then concatenate its pattern counts with the fixed partial plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Demand Completion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches secondary residual-demand optimization, but the record defines y* as an exact argmin and then also permits a heuristic output under the same notation. A source is needed to determine the intended exact or heuristic variant and support a corrected formulation without weakening it.

children.title: Restricted Integer Master Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Integer optimization over accumulated pattern pools.

assumptions_latex: A finite accumulated pattern pool \(P'\subseteq P\) is given.
Each \(p\in P'\) has cost \(c_p\) and incidence column \(a_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned feasible solution is valid for the full master, though pool restriction need not preserve global optimality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restricting a column-generation master to accumulated columns gives a finite integer master heuristic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer optimization over a finite pool previously produced by pricing or heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Solve, exactly or subject to a declared time or node limit,
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P'}c_px_p:\sum_{p\in P'}a_{ip}x_p\ge d_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ x\in\mathbb Z_+^{P'}\right\}.
\]
Return the best feasible incumbent \(x^{P'}\) found. Because \(P'\subseteq P\), extending \(x^{P'}\) by zeros yields a feasible solution of the full master. Its objective is an upper bound for the full minimization problem, but restricted-master optimality alone does not certify full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize integer pattern counts over the accumulated finite column pool; any feasible result is globally feasible, but may be suboptimal because patterns are missing.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Integer Master Heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the restricted integer master heuristic container. The feasibility and upper-bound claims are coherent for a minimization covering master, but no inspectable source is supplied for this accumulated-column-pool heuristic.

children.title: Branch-Price Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Exact tree search with pricing preserved at search nodes.

children.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching families whose restrictions remain representable in pricing.

assumptions_latex: At a search node \(v\), admissible columns form \(P_v\subseteq P\).
The node pricing oracle minimizes reduced cost over a representable pattern-feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A branching family is pricing-compatible when every child retains an exact pricing oracle over its restricted column set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: branch-and-price requires each branching restriction to be enforceable by the pricing subproblem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for branching decisions in a column-generation search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A branching disjunction at node \(v\) is pricing-compatible when it produces children \(u\in\mathcal C(v)\) satisfying \(P_v=\bigcup_{u\in\mathcal C(v)}P_u\), with mutually exclusive child restrictions for every integer solution, and when each set \(P_u\) is representable in the pricing model. In particular, an exact oracle must compute
\[
\min\{\bar c_u(p):p\in P_u\}
\]
and either return a minimizing admissible column or certify that the minimum is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching is pricing-compatible when its exhaustive child restrictions can be imposed in the pricing model and exact reduced-cost minimization remains available.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but the asserted union condition on child column sets is not a generally established characterization of exhaustive branching over integer solutions. A branch-and-price source is required to determine the correct hypotheses and distinguish partitioning solutions from restricting individual columns.

children.title: Generated-Pattern Branch-Bound Search
children.top_down_role: Exact branch-and-bound over generated pattern formulations.

children.title: Generated-Pattern Tree Search
children.top_down_role: Tree-search organization over dynamically generated pattern formulations.

assumptions_latex: The root node represents the original integer master.
Every nonterminal node is partitioned by an exhaustive valid branching disjunction.
Column generation solves each node LP to pricing optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search returns the least-cost integer incumbent after all nodes are fathomed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generated-pattern tree search is branch-and-bound with node relaxations solved by exact column generation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound whose node LPs are solved over implicit pattern families by pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal Q\) with the root and \(U=+\infty\). Select \(v\in\mathcal Q\), solve its restricted master, and price admissible patterns until no negative-reduced-cost column exists; record the resulting bound \(L_v\). Fathom \(v\) if it is infeasible or \(L_v\ge U\). If its solution is integer, update \(U\) and the incumbent. Otherwise create pricing-compatible children whose disjunction exhausts the integer solutions at \(v\), insert them into \(\mathcal Q\), and continue until \(\mathcal Q=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a branch-and-bound tree, completing column generation at every node, pruning by certified bounds, and updating the best integer cutting plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Pattern Tree Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits generated-pattern tree search, and the stated procedure is recognizable as branch-and-price with exact node pricing. No branch-and-price citation is provided for the node-processing, fathoming, and global-termination claims.

children.title: Nodewise Pricing Bounds
children.top_down_role: Pricing-supported bound information at individual search nodes.

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), the covering LP has right-hand side \(d_v\) and admissible patterns \(P_v\).
A vector \(\pi_v\ge0\) satisfies \(a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_v\le c_p\) for every \(p\in P_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every node-feasible integer solution has value at least \(d_v^{\mathsf T}\pi_v\), and at least \(\lceil d_v^{\mathsf T}\pi_v\rceil\) for integral objectives.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: LP weak duality plus exhaustive reduced-cost pricing supplies the standard node bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound certificate after exact nodewise pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If exact pricing certifies
\[
\min_{p\in P_v}\{c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_v\}\ge0,
\]
then \(\pi_v\) is feasible for the full node dual, including all ungenerated patterns. Weak duality gives the certified bound \(L_v=d_v^{\mathsf T}\pi_v\) on the node LP and hence on every node-feasible integer solution. When every integer solution has integral objective value, the strengthened integer bound \(\lceil L_v\rceil\) is valid for pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual vector plus exhaustive pricing that finds no negative reduced-cost pattern certifies an LP lower bound for every integer solution in that node.
knowledge_statements.title: Nodewise Pricing Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role is correct for this leaf, and the reduced-cost and weak-duality bound is internally coherent under the stated covering-dual convention. An inspectable source is still required for the branch-and-price node-bound certificate and its rounded integer bound.

children.title: Global Incumbent Certification
children.top_down_role: Certification of incumbent quality across the search tree.

assumptions_latex: An incumbent integer solution has objective value \(U<+\infty\).
The active and fathomed nodes form an exhaustive partition of all feasible integer solutions.
Every active node \(v\) has a valid lower bound \(L_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_v\ge U\) for every active node, the incumbent is globally optimal.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exhaustive branch-and-bound plus valid node lower bounds gives a global optimality certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate assembled from an incumbent and exhaustive nodewise bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^I\) be a feasible integer incumbent with \(c^{\mathsf T}x^I=U\). For every active node \(v\in\mathcal Q\), certify \(L_v\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for each integer solution represented by \(v\). Previously removed nodes must be certified infeasible, dominated by \(U\), or exhausted by valid branching. If
\[
\min_{v\in\mathcal Q}L_v\ge U,
\]
with the minimum over an empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\), then no feasible integer solution has value below \(U\), so \(x^I\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent is globally optimal when exhaustive branching is documented and every unresolved node has a certified lower bound no smaller than its value.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Incumbent Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits global incumbent certification, and the statement correctly includes exhaustive branching and valid disposition of removed nodes. No cited branch-and-bound or branch-and-price source supports the complete certification criterion.

children.title: Branch-Cut-Price Algorithm
children.top_down_role: Exact pattern generation combined with compatible valid inequalities.

children.title: Master-Space Cutting Planes
children.top_down_role: Inequality families separated in pattern-variable space.

assumptions_latex: The integer master set is \(X=\{x\in\mathbb Z_+^P:Ax\ge d\}\).
A current LP point \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_+^P\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A master-space cut is valid when \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) holds for all \(x\in X\), and separating when \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar x<\beta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid inequalities expressed directly in pattern-variable space.

source_refs.locator: 5.21 The integer hull and cutting planes p. 83

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A master-space cutting plane is an inequality
\[
\sum_{p\in P}\alpha_px_p\ge\beta
\]
that is valid for every \(x\in X\) but violated by the current relaxation point \(\bar x\). Adding it removes \(\bar x\) without removing any feasible integer cutting plan. In a column-generation formulation, validity concerns the full pattern index set \(P\), including columns not yet generated, so the coefficient \(\alpha_p\) must have a defined interpretation for every admissible pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master-space cut is a valid inequality in pattern variables that excludes the current fractional point while retaining every integer cutting plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Space Cutting Planes

source_witnesses.locator: 5.21 The integer hull and cutting planes p. 83

children.title: Cut-Column Compatibility Interface
children.top_down_role: Interaction between generated inequalities and pricing.

children.title: Cut-Compatible Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing subproblems that incorporate active master-space cuts.

assumptions_latex: Added master cuts are indexed by \(K\), with coefficient \(\gamma_{kp}\) for pattern \(p\).
Their current dual multipliers are \(\lambda_k\), and demand-row multipliers are \(\pi_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing is cut-compatible when it exactly minimizes the cut-adjusted reduced cost over every admissible pattern.

notation.meaning: Coefficient of pattern p in cut k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: every master row contributes its dual-weighted column coefficient to pricing reduced cost
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion ensuring added master cuts are represented exactly in the pricing objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every admissible pattern \(p\), define its cut-adjusted reduced cost by
\[
\bar c(p)=c_p-\sum_i\pi_i a_{ip}-\sum_{k\in K}\lambda_k\gamma_{kp},
\]
with signs changed consistently when a master row uses the opposite inequality convention. Pricing is cut-compatible if each \(\gamma_{kp}\) is computable from the pricing state and an exact oracle can minimize \(\bar c(p)\) over the node-admissible pattern set. A nonnegative oracle optimum then certifies dual feasibility for all latent columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing remains compatible with cuts when every latent pattern's cut coefficients are computable and the oracle minimizes the resulting full reduced cost exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Compatible Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits cut-compatible pricing, and the record explicitly acknowledges row-sign conventions. Nevertheless, no branch-cut-and-price source supports the reduced-cost formula, the required coefficient computability, or the resulting latent-column dual-feasibility certificate.

children.title: Column-Compatible Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation families suitable for dynamically generated columns.

assumptions_latex: The full master has an implicit pattern set \(P\), while the current restricted pool is \(P'\subseteq P\).
A separation procedure observes the current restricted-master solution \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separation is column-compatible when every returned cut is valid over \(P\) and supplies coefficients for all future columns.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separation in a dynamic-column master must define valid coefficients for generated and future columns
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for separating inequalities while the master column set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A separator is column-compatible if, whenever it returns a violated inequality
\[
\sum_{p\in P}\gamma_k(p)x_p\ge\beta_k,
\]
the inequality is valid for every integer solution over the full set \(P\), not merely over \(P'\), and the mapping \(p\mapsto\gamma_k(p)\) is defined for every future admissible pattern. The separator may evaluate violation using \(\bar x_p=0\) for \(p\notin P'\), but its validity test and coefficient rule must not depend on the current pool being complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation is column-compatible when its cuts are globally valid and provide a computable coefficient for every generated or future pattern.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Compatible Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits column-compatible separation, and the distinction between validity over the full pattern family and evaluation on the restricted pool is coherent. An inspectable branch-cut-and-price source is required for this compatibility criterion.

children.title: Incompatibility Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Cases where cuts obstruct tractable or valid column generation.

assumptions_latex: A master cut has coefficients \(\gamma_p\) and dual multiplier \(\lambda\).
Pricing either omits \(-\lambda\gamma_p\) or cannot compute \(\gamma_p\) for latent patterns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Omitting unavailable cut coefficients can invalidate reduced-cost optimality and every bound derived from it.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost used by incompatible pricing

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: omitted dual-row contributions produce incorrect reduced costs and destroy column-generation certificates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by cuts whose latent-column coefficients are absent from pricing or separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a latent pattern \(q\) has \(c_q=1\), \(a_q^{\mathsf T}\pi=1\), \(\gamma_q=1\), and \(\lambda=1\). Pricing that ignores the cut reports
\[
\widetilde c(q)=c_q-a_q^{\mathsf T}\pi=0,
\]
although the correct reduced cost is
\[
\bar c(q)=c_q-a_q^{\mathsf T}\pi-\lambda\gamma_q=-1.
\]
Thus it can falsely terminate while an improving column exists. The restricted-master value is then not a valid full-master bound, so pruning or global optimality claims based on that termination may be incorrect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If pricing omits a cut's coefficient for latent patterns, it may miss improving columns, making node bounds, pruning decisions, and optimality claims invalid.
knowledge_statements.title: Incompatibility Failure Modes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role is appropriate, and the numerical example consistently demonstrates the danger of omitting a dual-row contribution under its chosen reduced-cost convention. No source establishes that convention or supports the downstream claims about invalid bounds, pruning, and optimality certification.

children.title: Explicit-State Exact Optimization Family
children.top_down_role: Integer optimization over explicit or compressed state-space formulations.

children.title: Integer Arc-Flow Optimization
children.top_down_role: Exact optimization over path-based pattern networks.

assumptions_latex: The directed acyclic state network represents every feasible one-stock cutting pattern as an \(s\)-\(t\) path and no infeasible pattern as such a path.
All demands \(b_i\) and arc multiplicities are integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal integral flow gives a minimum-stock cutting plan, and its decomposition into \(s\)-\(t\) paths gives the selected patterns.

notation.meaning: Directed acyclic pattern network with source and sink
Number of items of type i represented by arc a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact arc-flow formulation for one-dimensional cutting stock on an acyclic pattern network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed acyclic network whose \(s\)-\(t\) paths encode exactly the feasible patterns for stock length \(L\). For each arc \(a\), let \(q_{ia}\in\mathbb Z_+\) be its contribution to item type \(i\), and let \(f_a\in\mathbb Z_+\). Integer arc-flow optimization minimizes the total flow leaving \(s\), subject to flow conservation at every \(v\in V\setminus\{s,t\}\) and demand coverage \(\sum_{a\in A}q_{ia}f_a\ge b_i\) for every item type \(i\). Every feasible integral flow decomposes into encoded \(s\)-\(t\) paths, so its objective and produced item counts equal those of the corresponding integer pattern solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the number of stock paths carried by an integral flow whose arc contributions cover every item demand; path decomposition recovers an equivalent cutting-pattern solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Arc-Flow Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the arc-flow leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no cited source supports the cutting-stock-specific network encoding, demand accounting, or equivalence with the complete integer pattern model.

children.title: Compact-Model Branch-Cut Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Exact search over item- or stock-indexed formulations.

children.title: Item-Indexed Branch-Cut
children.top_down_role: Exact tree search over item-indexed compact formulations.

assumptions_latex: At most \(U\) stock rolls are available, with \(U\) a valid upper bound.
Each demanded item copy must be assigned to exactly one used roll, and each roll has capacity \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with no open branch-and-bound node returns a minimum-roll feasible cutting plan.

notation.meaning: Binary assignment of item copy j to roll k
Binary indicator that roll k is used

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-cut for a binary formulation indexed by individual demanded item copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given item copies \(j\in J\), lengths \(w_j\), stock length \(L\), and roll indices \(k=1,\ldots,U\), solve \(\min\sum_k y_k\) over binary variables satisfying \(\sum_k x_{jk}=1\), \(x_{jk}\le y_k\), and \(\sum_j w_jx_{jk}\le Ly_k\). Initialize branch-and-bound with the linear relaxation. At each node, separate violated valid inequalities for the item-indexed packing polytope, add them, and reoptimize; if the solution remains fractional, branch on an unfixed \(x_{jk}\) or \(y_k\). Prune by infeasibility or incumbent bounds, and output the best integral assignment after all nodes are closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-cut assigns every item copy to a capacity-feasible used roll, repeatedly adding valid inequalities and branching until optimality is certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Item-Indexed Branch-Cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the branch-and-cut leaf, and the compact item-copy formulation is coherent. A cutting-stock source is required for this named formulation and its asserted valid-inequality separation procedure.

children.title: Stock-Indexed Branch-Cut
children.top_down_role: Exact tree search over stock-indexed compact formulations.

assumptions_latex: The indexed stock set has size \(U\), where \(U\) is a valid upper bound on the optimum.
Variables and linking constraints exclude production on unused stock rolls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhausting the branch-and-cut tree certifies that the incumbent uses the minimum possible number of rolls.

notation.meaning: Number of type-i items cut from indexed roll k
Binary use variable for indexed roll k
Demand and item length for type i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-cut for a compact formulation indexed by candidate stock rolls and item types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given lengths \(w_i\), demands \(b_i\), stock length \(L\), and rolls \(k=1,\ldots,U\), solve \(\min\sum_k y_k\) with \(z_{ik}\in\mathbb Z_+\), \(y_k\in\{0,1\}\), \(\sum_k z_{ik}\ge b_i\), and \(\sum_i w_i z_{ik}\le Ly_k\). Begin from its linear relaxation, impose symmetry-breaking constraints on identically indexed rolls, and at each node separate violated valid inequalities. Reoptimize after adding cuts; otherwise branch on a fractional \(y_k\) or \(z_{ik}\). Prune infeasible or bound-dominated nodes and return the best integral solution when no node remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-cut distributes type-level item counts among indexed stock rolls, adding cuts and branching until the minimum number of rolls is certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Stock-Indexed Branch-Cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the stock-indexed branch-and-cut leaf, but the cutting-stock-specific formulation, symmetry-breaking constraints, and cut families have no supporting citation.

children.title: Compact-Model Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation of valid inequalities for compact cutting-stock models.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation is a rational polyhedron \(P=\{x:Ax\le d\}\).
The selected inequality family is valid for every feasible integral cutting plan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned violated inequality may be added without removing any feasible integer solution; failure to find one is conclusive only for the searched family.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact separation step within compact cutting-stock branch-and-cut models.

source_refs.locator: 5.21 The integer hull and cutting planes p. 83
Section 4.6. Separation and Optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fractional node solution \(\bar x\in P\), a compact-model separation routine searches a prescribed valid-inequality family for coefficients \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying \(\alpha^T x\le\beta\) for every feasible integral cutting plan but \(\alpha^T\bar x>\beta\). If such an inequality is found, add it to \(P\) and reoptimize. If none exists, report that \(\bar x\) satisfies every inequality in the searched family; this does not imply membership in the integer hull unless that family completely describes the hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fractional solution, find a valid inequality it violates, add the cut, and reoptimize; nonseparation is meaningful only relative to the searched family.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Model Cut Separation

source_witnesses.locator: 5.21 The integer hull and cutting planes p. 83
Section 4.6. Separation and Optimization p. 93

children.title: Cutting-Stock Integrality-Gap Theory
children.top_down_role: The relationship between the pattern relaxation, integer plans, round-up properties, and exceptional instances.

children.title: Gilmore-Gomory Relaxation Bound
children.top_down_role: The principal fractional benchmark for one-dimensional cutting stock.

children.title: Fractional Pattern Optimum
children.top_down_role: The LP benchmark supplied by complete column generation.

assumptions_latex: The pattern set contains every integer vector \(a\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) satisfying \(\sum_i w_i a_i\le L\).
Demands satisfy \(b_i\in\mathbb Z_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fractional pattern optimum is the linear-programming lower bound \(z_{m LP}\) on the number of stock rolls.

notation.meaning: Set of all feasible one-roll cutting patterns
Multiplicity of item type i in pattern p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gilmore-Gomory covering relaxation with the complete feasible-pattern set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For item lengths \(w_i\), demands \(b_i\), and stock length \(L\), let \(\mathcal P=\{a\in\mathbb Z_+^m:\sum_i w_i a_i\le L\}\). The fractional pattern optimum is
\[z_{\rm LP}:=\min\left\{\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}x_p:\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_{ip}x_p\ge b_i\ \text{for all }i,\ x_p\ge0\ \text{for all }p\right\}.\]
Because the complete pattern set is used, exact column generation computes this value when pricing is solved exactly and terminates with no negative-reduced-cost pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fractional pattern optimum minimizes total fractional pattern usage while covering every demand, using all feasible one-roll patterns; it is the complete column-generation bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Pattern Optimum

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the fractional complete-pattern optimum, but no source with an inspectable locator supports either the Gilmore–Gomory formulation or the exact-column-generation termination claim.

children.title: Integer Pattern Optimum
children.top_down_role: The integral benchmark used for gap analysis.

assumptions_latex: The pattern set contains every feasible one-stock integer cutting pattern.
Demand overproduction is allowed, as in the covering formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer pattern optimum \(z_{m IP}\) is the minimum number of stock rolls in a pattern-based cutting plan.

notation.meaning: Number of rolls cut according to pattern p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer counterpart of the complete Gilmore-Gomory pattern covering relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With the complete pattern set \(\mathcal P\) and pattern coefficients \(a_{ip}\), the integer pattern optimum is
\[z_{\rm IP}:=\min\left\{\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}x_p:\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_{ip}x_p\ge b_i\ \text{for every }i,\ x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\ \text{for every }p\right\}.\]
Thus \(z_{\rm LP}\le z_{\rm IP}\), where \(z_{\rm LP}\) is obtained by replacing integrality with nonnegativity. Any feasible integer vector specifies a multiset of stock patterns, and its objective is exactly the number of rolls used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer pattern optimum is the fewest whole stock patterns whose combined production covers all demands; it is at least the corresponding fractional optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Pattern Optimum

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent and matches the integer pattern benchmark, but the complete-pattern covering model and its interpretation lack a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Integer Round-Up Properties
children.top_down_role: Named round-up principles and their validity boundaries.

children.title: Integer Round-Up Property
children.top_down_role: The exact round-up principle and its structured instance classes.

assumptions_latex: Both optima use the same complete pattern set and covering constraints.
The instance has finite integer demands and positive item lengths not exceeding \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance has the integer round-up property exactly when \(z_{\rm IP}=\lceil z_{\rm LP}\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instancewise integer round-up property for the one-dimensional Gilmore-Gomory relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A one-dimensional cutting-stock instance has the integer round-up property if
\[z_{\rm IP}=\left\lceil z_{\rm LP}\right\rceil,\]
where \(z_{\rm LP}\) and \(z_{\rm IP}\) are respectively the fractional and integer optima of the same complete-pattern covering formulation. Since \(z_{\rm IP}\) is integral and \(z_{\rm LP}\le z_{\rm IP}\), the reverse inequality \(z_{\rm IP}\ge\lceil z_{\rm LP}\rceil\) always holds; the property therefore asserts the checkable upper bound \(z_{\rm IP}\le\lceil z_{\rm LP}\rceil\). A class has the property when this equality holds for every instance in that class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An instance has the integer round-up property when its integer pattern optimum equals the ceiling of its fractional pattern optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Round-Up Property

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The instancewise equality is the standard form of the integer round-up property and the property kind fits. A source is still required, particularly because the node role also calls for structured validity classes that the record does not identify.

children.title: Modified Integer Round-Up Property
children.top_down_role: The weakened round-up principle beyond exact validity.

assumptions_latex: The fractional and integer values arise from the same complete-pattern covering formulation.
The optimum values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The modified integer round-up property is the bound \(z_{\rm IP}\le\lceil z_{\rm LP}\rceil+1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instancewise one-unit weakening of the exact integer round-up property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A cutting-stock instance has the modified integer round-up property if
\[z_{\rm IP}\le\left\lceil z_{\rm LP}\right\rceil+1.\]
Equivalently, its additive gap satisfies \(\Delta=z_{\rm IP}-z_{\rm LP}\le 1+\lceil z_{\rm LP}\rceil-z_{\rm LP}<2\). Every instance with the exact integer round-up property satisfies this modified property, but the converse can fail when \(z_{\rm IP}=\lceil z_{\rm LP}\rceil+1\). A family has the modified property only if the displayed inequality holds uniformly for all of its instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The modified round-up property permits the integer pattern optimum to exceed the ceiling of the fractional optimum by at most one roll.
knowledge_statements.title: Modified Integer Round-Up Property

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated one-roll weakening and its gap calculation are internally consistent, but an authoritative source is needed to validate that this is the intended cutting-stock meaning and scope of the modified integer round-up property.

children.title: Round-Up Counterexample Families
children.top_down_role: Exceptional instances delimiting round-up claims.

assumptions_latex: Each instance uses the complete-pattern fractional and integer covering models.
The family contains instances of increasing size or demand rather than duplicate encodings of one instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive values of \(e(I)=z_{\rm IP}(I)-\lceil z_{\rm LP}(I)\rceil\) certify failure of exact round-up; values at least \(2\) also refute modified round-up.

notation.meaning: Integer excess above the rounded fractional bound
A parameterized family of cutting-stock instances
Fractional and integer pattern optima of instance I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic boundary for families refuting exact or modified integer round-up claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(I\), define the round-up excess by \(e(I):=z_{\rm IP}(I)-\lceil z_{\rm LP}(I)\rceil\). A parameterized family \(\{I_k\}_{k\ge1}\) is an exact-round-up counterexample family when \(e(I_k)\ge1\) for every \(k\); it refutes any universal integer round-up assertion over a class containing that family. If \(e(I_k)\ge2\) for some member, that member also violates the modified integer round-up property. A claimed uniform additive bound \(C\) fails on the family when \(z_{\rm IP}(I_k)-z_{\rm LP}(I_k)>C\) for some \(k\), and is unboundedly false when these gaps diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counterexample families are parameterized instances with positive excess over the rounded fractional bound; excess of at least two also defeats the modified property.
knowledge_statements.title: Round-Up Counterexample Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure thresholds follow from the stated round-up definitions and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate. However, the plural terminal calls for counterexample families, while the record supplies only a generic criterion and cites no published family.

children.title: Pattern-Relaxation Integrality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Additive and structural gap regimes between fractional and integer pattern solutions.

children.title: Additive Gap Analysis
children.top_down_role: Gap organization by additive deviation from the fractional bound.

assumptions_latex: The complete-pattern linear and integer programs are both feasible and have finite optima.
Both programs use identical pattern coefficients and demand constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additive gap is \(\Delta(I)=z_{\rm IP}(I)-z_{\rm LP}(I)\ge0\), and a class bound is the supremum of these differences.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute, rather than multiplicative, gap for the complete pattern relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a cutting-stock instance \(I\), its additive pattern-relaxation gap is
\[\Delta(I):=z_{\rm IP}(I)-z_{\rm LP}(I).\]
Because the fractional feasible region contains every integer feasible solution, \(\Delta(I)\ge0\). For a class \(\mathcal C\), the uniform additive gap is \(\Delta(\mathcal C):=\sup_{I\in\mathcal C}\Delta(I)\), possibly infinite. The rounded excess \(z_{\rm IP}(I)-\lceil z_{\rm LP}(I)\rceil\) is a distinct integer-valued statistic: exact integer round-up is equivalent to rounded excess zero, whereas \(\Delta(I)\) retains the fractional part of \(z_{\rm LP}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive gap analysis measures the absolute difference between integer and fractional pattern optima, either instancewise or by the supremum over an instance class.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Gap Analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-gap definition is internally consistent, distinguishes the rounded excess correctly, and fits the analysis leaf. It nevertheless has no cutting-stock source with a specific locator.

children.title: Integrality-Gap Instance Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Instance classes used to establish or challenge integrality behavior.

children.title: Structured Gap Families
children.top_down_role: Systematically constructed instance classes exhibiting characteristic gap behavior.

assumptions_latex: Every family member is specified by explicit item lengths, demands, and stock length.
The defining restrictions are invariant under relabeling item types.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family gap profile is the function \(g(k)=z_{\rm IP}(I_k)-z_{\rm LP}(I_k)\), analyzed under the stated structural restrictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized subfamilies defined by explicit arithmetic or combinatorial restrictions on cutting-stock data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A structured gap family is a parameterized collection \(\{I_k\}_{k\in K}\) of cutting-stock instances for which an explicit predicate \(S(I_k)\) fixes nontrivial restrictions on lengths, demands, the number of item types, or admissible patterns. Its additive gap profile is
\[g(k):=z_{\rm IP}(I_k)-z_{\rm LP}(I_k).\]
The structure must be stated independently of the observed optimum values; merely selecting instances because their gaps are large does not define a structured family. A uniform family result specifies a constant or function \(B(k)\) such that \(g(k)\le B(k)\) for every admissible parameter \(k\), or supplies members violating such a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured gap family has explicit data restrictions independent of its observed gap, permitting uniform analysis of integer-minus-fractional optimum values.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured Gap Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is logically coherent, but it is an uncited meta-definition rather than sourced knowledge about recognized structured cutting-stock gap families. Sources are needed to fix the intended taxonomy and provide actual families.

children.title: Exceptional Gap Instances
children.top_down_role: Atypical instances challenging expected integrality behavior.

assumptions_latex: A reference class \(\mathcal C\) and a precise baseline gap claim for that class are fixed.
Integer and fractional optima are computed from the complete-pattern formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exceptional instance is certified by feasible primal solutions and valid lower bounds establishing violation of the chosen baseline claim.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification of instances lying outside a specified round-up or additive-gap baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a reference class \(\mathcal C\) and a baseline claim \(\Delta(I)\le B(I)\). An instance \(I\in\mathcal C\) is exceptional relative to that claim when
\[\Delta(I)=z_{\rm IP}(I)-z_{\rm LP}(I)>B(I).\]
A verifiable certificate consists of an exact fractional optimum, an exact integer optimum, and independently checkable primal and dual or enumeration evidence attaining and bounding those values. For the exact integer round-up baseline, exceptionality is equivalently certified by \(z_{\rm IP}(I)\ge\lceil z_{\rm LP}(I)\rceil+1\). The adjective exceptional has no mathematical content until \(\mathcal C\), \(B\), and the formulation used for both optima are specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exceptional gap instance violates a specified baseline bound, with exact fractional and integer values certified by checkable upper- and lower-bound evidence.
knowledge_statements.title: Exceptional Gap Instances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record makes exceptionality relative to an arbitrary baseline and discusses certification without identifying any exceptional instance. A domain source is required to establish the intended baseline, examples, and whether this leaf should contain a certificate rather than a definition or counterexample record.

children.title: Gap-Boundary Counterexamples
children.top_down_role: Instances marking limits of proposed gap patterns or round-up behavior.

assumptions_latex: One-dimensional stock has length \(L=10\).
There are three labeled item types with lengths \(\ell_1=\ell_2=\ell_3=4\) and demands \(b_1=b_2=b_3=1\).
The pattern relaxation permits nonnegative real pattern multiplicities, whereas the integer model requires nonnegative integer multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}=3/2\), \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=2\), and hence \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}-z_{\mathrm{LP}}=1/2\), although \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=\lceil z_{\mathrm{LP}}\rceil\).

notation.meaning: Optimal values of the pattern LP and integer cutting-stock model.
Pattern cutting one item of each of types i and j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite instance marking the boundary between a positive raw gap and failure of the rounded gap property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the three feasible pair patterns \(p_{12},p_{13},p_{23}\), each using length \(8\); no stock can contain three items. The fractional assignment \(x_{12}=x_{13}=x_{23}=1/2\) covers every demand and uses \(3/2\) stocks. Summing the three covering constraints shows that every fractional solution uses at least \(3/2\) stocks. An integer solution cannot use one stock because it contains at most two demanded items, while two stocks suffice. Thus the unrounded integrality gap is positive, but rounding the relaxation value removes it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three equal items fit only two per stock: the pattern LP uses 1.5 stocks, the integer model uses 2, and the rounded gap is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Boundary Counterexamples

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the exact leaf, and the stated LP and integer values are mathematically plausible. However, no citation or inspectable locator supports the instance, and the statement includes argument text deriving the bounds, contrary to the no-proof requirement. Source-backed verification is required before the mathematical claim can be accepted.

children.title: Operational Cutting Constraint Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Cutting-specific restrictions retained in the chapter and broader operational couplings routed to neighboring chapters.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: An Improved Typology of Cutting and Packing Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Special cutting-and-packing problems and application literature
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: An Improved Typology of Cutting and Packing Problems

children.title: Pattern-Usage Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Cutting-plan variants with restrictions on the pattern portfolio.

children.title: Pattern Activation Complexity Models
children.top_down_role: Models controlling the number or cost of distinct patterns.

children.title: Setup-Cost Models
children.top_down_role: Cutting-stock models charging costs for activating distinct patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite set of feasible cutting patterns.
Pattern \(p\) has multiplicity \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\), activation indicator \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\), valid bound \(U_p\), and setup cost \(s_p\ge 0\).
Demand constraints are \(\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}x_p\ge b_i\) for every item type \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible setup-cost model minimizes \(\sum_{p\in P}c_px_p+\sum_{p\in P}s_py_p\) subject to demand coverage and \(0\le x_p\le U_py_p\) for all \(p\in P\).

notation.meaning: Number of times pattern p is executed.
Indicator that pattern p is activated.
Variable and fixed setup costs of pattern p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-charge pattern formulation with a valid activation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(p\in P\), impose \(0\le x_p\le U_py_p\). Because \(y_p\) is binary, any positive use of pattern \(p\) forces \(y_p=1\), while an inactive pattern has \(x_p=0\). The objective \[\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P}c_px_p+\sum_{p\in P}s_py_p:\ \sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}x_p\ge b_i\ \text{for all }i,\ 0\le x_p\le U_py_p\ \text{for all }p\right\}\] therefore charges \(s_p\) once whenever pattern \(p\) is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary activation variable links each used pattern to a one-time setup charge, while integer multiplicities cover item demands.
knowledge_statements.title: Setup-Cost Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Setup-Cost Models, and the fixed-charge activation formulation is internally coherent. No source reference or specific locator is supplied for the cutting-stock setup-cost model or the validity requirements on the bounds U_p.

children.title: Distinct-Pattern Minimization
children.top_down_role: Objectives targeting a small number of distinct patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite feasible-pattern set and \(a_{ip}\) is the number of items of type \(i\) in pattern \(p\).
Demands are \(b_i\in\mathbb Z_+\), multiplicities satisfy \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\), and activations satisfy \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\).
Each \(U_p\) is a valid finite upper bound on \(x_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal value \(\min\sum_{p\in P}y_p\) is the minimum number of distinct patterns required to cover all demands.

notation.meaning: Multiplicity and activation indicator of pattern p.
Number of type-i items produced by pattern p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality minimization over the support of a cutting plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distinct-pattern minimization is represented by \[\min\left\{\sum_{p\in P}y_p:\ \sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}x_p\ge b_i\ \text{for all }i,\ 0\le x_p\le U_py_p\ \text{for all }p,\ x_p\in\mathbb Z_+,\ y_p\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\] At every feasible solution, \(x_p>0\) implies \(y_p=1\). Conversely, an optimal solution can take \(y_p=0\) whenever \(x_p=0\), so the objective equals the support cardinality \(\lvert\{p:x_p>0\}\rvert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize binary pattern activations linked to integer pattern uses; the objective equals the number of distinct patterns in the plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Distinct-Pattern Minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the objective correctly models support cardinality under the stated linking assumptions. The record has no cited source or inspectable locator supporting this cutting-stock formulation.

children.title: Pattern-Activation Limits
children.top_down_role: Restrictions limiting how many distinct patterns may be activated.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite feasible-pattern set.
Pattern multiplicities are \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\), activations are \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x_p\le U_py_p\) uses valid bounds \(U_p\).
The permitted number of active patterns is \(K\in\mathbb Z_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(\sum_{p\in P}y_p\le K\) is equivalent to requiring \(\lvert\{p\in P:x_p>0\}\rvert\le K\) in an activation-minimal feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A global cardinality bound on the support of the cutting plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pattern-activation limit is imposed by \[x_p\le U_py_p\quad\text{for every }p\in P,\qquad \sum_{p\in P}y_p\le K.\] The linking inequalities ensure that every used pattern is counted. If activation has no separate operational meaning, unused activations may be set to zero without changing \(x\); consequently feasibility is equivalent to the existence of a cutting plan whose positive-multiplicity support contains at most \(K\) patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Link pattern use to binary indicators and bound their sum by K to permit at most K distinct patterns.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Activation Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Pattern-Activation Limits, and the existential support-cardinality interpretation is appropriately qualified by the absence of separate operational meaning for unused activations. No source or specific locator is provided.

children.title: Pattern Usage-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on how often particular patterns may be used.

children.title: Pattern Frequency Limits
children.top_down_role: General restrictions on pattern-use frequency.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite set of feasible cutting patterns.
For each \(p\in P\), the allowed frequency set is described by integers \(0\le \ell_p\le u_p\).
Pattern use is \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\) and activation is \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete frequency restriction is \(\ell_py_p\le x_p\le u_py_p\) for every \(p\in P\).

notation.meaning: Multiplicity and activation indicator of pattern p.
Minimum and maximum frequency when pattern p is active.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided conditional bounds on each pattern multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every pattern \(p\in P\), impose \[\ell_py_p\le x_p\le u_py_p,\qquad x_p\in\mathbb Z_+,\qquad y_p\in\{0,1\}.\] If \(y_p=0\), these inequalities force \(x_p=0\). If \(y_p=1\), they require \(x_p\in\{\ell_p,\ell_p+1,\ldots,u_p\}\). Thus the admissible frequency set is exactly \(\{0\}\cup\{\ell_p,\ldots,u_p\}\), with the zero value representing nonactivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each pattern is either unused or executed an integer number of times between its specified lower and upper frequencies.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Frequency Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the two-sided activation formulation is internally consistent. The record lacks a source and inspectable locator establishing this frequency-limit model in the cutting-stock context.

children.title: Lower Usage Bounds
children.top_down_role: Minimum-use requirements for activated patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite feasible-pattern set.
Pattern multiplicities satisfy \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\), with activation indicators \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\).
Each active pattern \(p\) has a prescribed minimum run length \(\ell_p\in\mathbb Z_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower-usage condition is \(x_p\ge \ell_py_p\) together with an activation link forcing \(x_p=0\) when \(y_p=0\).

notation.meaning: Number of executions of pattern p.
Activation indicator and minimum active run length.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum run-length restriction conditional on pattern activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a valid finite upper bound \(U_p\) and impose \[\ell_py_p\le x_p\le U_py_p,\qquad x_p\in\mathbb Z_+,\qquad y_p\in\{0,1\},\quad p\in P.\] These constraints give the disjunction \(x_p=0\) or \(x_p\ge\ell_p\). When \(\ell_p=0\), the lower bound is vacuous; when \(\ell_p\ge1\), activating pattern \(p\) commits the cutting plan to at least \(\ell_p\) executions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activated pattern must be run at least its minimum batch size; an inactive pattern is used zero times.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower Usage Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Lower Usage Bounds, and the formulation correctly includes an upper activation link so that inactivity forces zero use. No cited source or specific locator supports the model or its minimum-run interpretation.

children.title: Upper Usage Bounds
children.top_down_role: Maximum-use restrictions for selected patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite feasible-pattern set.
Pattern multiplicities satisfy \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\).
Each pattern has a prescribed finite capacity \(u_p\in\mathbb Z_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The upper-usage condition is \(0\le x_p\le u_p\) for every \(p\in P\), or \(x_p\le u_py_p\) when activation is modeled explicitly.

notation.meaning: Number of executions of pattern p.
Maximum permitted executions of pattern p.
Optional activation indicator for pattern p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-pattern capacity restriction on cutting-plan multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without explicit activation variables, impose \[x_p\in\{0,1,\ldots,u_p\}\quad\text{for every }p\in P.\] If activation is represented by \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\), the conditional form is \(0\le x_p\le u_py_p\). It simultaneously forces \(x_p=0\) for an inactive pattern and caps an active pattern at \(u_p\) executions. These bounds may encode tool life, pattern availability, or production-policy limits, but their mathematical role is identical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cap the integer multiplicity of every pattern, optionally using a binary variable to make the cap conditional on activation.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper Usage Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Upper Usage Bounds, and both the direct integer cap and optional activation-linked form are coherent. The operational interpretations and cutting-stock specialization have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Cutting-Process Restrictions
children.top_down_role: One-dimensional process constraints affecting feasible patterns.

children.title: Cutting-Loss Usability Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Pattern feasibility modified by cutting loss or usable-length requirements.

children.title: Kerf-Loss Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Pattern feasibility accounting for material consumed by cuts.

assumptions_latex: A stock bar has usable length \(L>0\), and item type \(i\) has length \(\ell_i>0\).
A pattern contains \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) pieces and uses a saw kerf of width \(\kappa\ge0\) per separating cut.
Pieces are arranged linearly, so \(q\) produced pieces require \(\max\{q-1,0\}\) internal separating cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pattern is kerf-feasible exactly when \(\sum_i\ell_i a_i+\kappa\max\{\sum_i a_i-1,0\}\le L\).

notation.meaning: Number of type-i pieces in the pattern.
Material width lost at each separating cut.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional kerf accounting under the internal-separating-cut convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q=\sum_i a_i\). Under the convention that adjacent output pieces require one material-consuming separating cut and no kerf is charged at stock ends, total consumed length is \[\sum_i\ell_i a_i+\kappa\max\{q-1,0\}.\] Therefore a pattern belongs to the kerf-feasible pattern set precisely when this quantity does not exceed \(L\). If an operation charges end cuts or uses a different cut sequence, its corresponding cut count must replace \(\max\{q-1,0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add one kerf width for each internal separating cut; item length plus kerf loss must not exceed stock length.
knowledge_statements.title: Kerf-Loss Restrictions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Kerf-Loss Restrictions, but the exact q-1 kerf count depends on the cutting and end-cut convention. No source or locator verifies that convention, so the claimed exact feasibility formula cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Trim-Allowance Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Pattern feasibility under permitted or required trim allowances.

assumptions_latex: A stock bar has length \(L>0\), and pattern \(a\) contains \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) pieces of length \(\ell_i\).
Required left and right trim allowances are \(\tau^-\ge0\) and \(\tau^+\ge0\).
The cutting process incurs a known pattern-dependent loss \(k(a)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pattern \(a\) satisfies the trim allowance exactly when \(\tau^-+\sum_i\ell_i a_i+k(a)+\tau^+\le L\).

notation.meaning: Required trim at the two stock ends.
Pattern-dependent cutting loss, including any applicable kerf.
Multiplicity vector of produced item types.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional feasibility with mandatory material reserved at both stock ends.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mandatory trim consumes \(\tau^-+\tau^+\) units independently of demanded output. Hence the pattern-feasibility predicate is \[\tau^-+\sum_i\ell_i a_i+k(a)+\tau^+\le L.\] Equivalently, demanded pieces and process loss may occupy at most \(L-\tau^--\tau^+\). If trim differs by stock type, the same condition is indexed by that type; trim material is not counted as produced demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reserve mandatory trim at both stock ends; pieces and cutting losses must fit in the remaining stock length.
knowledge_statements.title: Trim-Allowance Restrictions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Trim-Allowance Restrictions, and the formula is coherent under the stated additive-loss convention. No source or inspectable locator supports that convention or establishes that k(a) excludes the separately represented end trims.

children.title: Minimum Usable-Length Requirements
children.top_down_role: Restrictions requiring a minimum usable portion of each stock object.

assumptions_latex: For a feasible cutting pattern \(a\), residual length is \(r(a)=L-\sum_i\ell_i a_i-k(a)\ge0\).
A retained remnant has indicator \(u(a)\in\{0,1\}\).
The minimum reusable length is \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A retained remnant must satisfy \(r(a)\ge\rho\); with an indicator, this is enforced by \(\rho u(a)\le r(a)\le Lu(a)\).

notation.meaning: Residual length after producing pattern a.
Indicator that the residual is retained as usable stock.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility threshold for retaining residual material as a reusable remnant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When every positive residual must either be retained as reusable stock or excluded from the admissible pattern set, impose \[\rho u(a)\le r(a)\le Lu(a),\qquad u(a)\in\{0,1\}.\] Thus \(u(a)=0\) forces \(r(a)=0\), while \(u(a)=1\) requires \(r(a)\in[\rho,L]\). If disposal of short residuals is allowed, introduce a discarded-residual variable separately; the inequality \(r(a)\ge\rho\) then applies only to the retained portion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A leftover may be retained as reusable stock only when its length reaches the prescribed minimum threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Usable-Length Requirements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but rho u(a) <= r(a) <= L u(a) forces zero residual whenever the remnant is not retained. That is valid only under the record's restrictive no-disposal convention; ordinary models may permit discarded positive residuals. A source with a specific locator is required to establish the intended convention and formulation.

children.title: Cutting-Operation Feasibility Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Pattern restrictions induced by cutting operations or equipment.

children.title: Cut-Count Limits
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on the number of cutting operations within a pattern.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a set of candidate cutting patterns.
Each pattern \(p\) has a nonnegative integer cut count \(c_p\).
The equipment permits at most \(C\in\mathbb Z_+\) cuts per stock unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The admissible pattern set is \(P_C=\{p\in P:c_p\le C\}\), and every used pattern must belong to \(P_C\).

notation.meaning: Number of cutting operations required by pattern p.
Maximum permitted cuts per stock unit.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-stock operational limit using a specified cut-count convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[P_C=\{p\in P:c_p\le C\}.\] A cutting plan with multiplicities \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\) satisfies the cut-count restriction when \(x_p=0\) for every \(p\notin P_C\). Equivalently, pattern generation may retain only columns satisfying \(c_p\le C\). The value \(c_p\) must be computed under the applicable process convention, since guillotine, sequential, and bundled cuts can assign different counts to the same output multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use only patterns whose required number of cutting operations does not exceed the equipment's per-stock cut limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Count Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Cut-Count Limits, and filtering the pattern set by c_p <= C is coherent. The substantive meaning of c_p varies with the cutting process, and no source or locator specifies or supports the applicable counting convention.

children.title: Tooling-Feasible Patterns
children.top_down_role: Pattern families compatible with available tooling configurations.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a candidate pattern set, and pattern \(p\) has nonnegative tooling-resource vector \(t(p)\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
Available tooling capacity per stock operation is \(h\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
Resource inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tooling-feasible pattern set is \(P_T=\{p\in P:t(p)\le h\}\).

notation.meaning: Tooling resources required to execute pattern p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract multi-resource predicate for pattern-level tooling feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pattern is tooling-feasible precisely when every required tooling resource respects its capacity: \[p\in P_T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad t_j(p)\le h_j\ \text{for every }j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] Consequently, a cutting plan with multiplicities \(x_p\in\mathbb Z_+\) is tooling-feasible only if \(x_p=0\) for all \(p\notin P_T\). Discrete compatibility requirements may be included as components of the predicate defining \(P_T\), rather than represented by numeric capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pattern is admissible only when all tools, slots, or other tooling resources it requires are available within capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Tooling-Feasible Patterns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Tooling-Feasible Patterns, and the componentwise capacity predicate is internally consistent as an abstract model. No cited source or inspectable locator supports this tooling-resource representation or its cutting-stock interpretation.

children.title: Equipment-Capacity Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Pattern restrictions induced by cutting-equipment capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Equipment-Capacity Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-capacity feasibility for cutting patterns assigned to equipment and periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{pkt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the number of executions of cutting pattern \(p\) on equipment \(k\) in period \(t\). If one execution consumes \(r_{hpk}\ge 0\) units of equipment resource \(h\), and \(R_{hkt}\ge 0\) units are available, equipment-capacity feasibility requires
\[\sum_p r_{hpk}x_{pkt}\le R_{hkt}\qquad\text{for every }h,k,t.\]
Resources may represent processing time, blade travel, machine cycles, or another additive equipment limit; only patterns feasible on equipment \(k\) may have \(x_{pkt}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total resource consumed by assigned pattern executions cannot exceed each equipment resource’s available capacity in any period.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{pkt}\in\mathbb Z_+\)
\(r_{hpk}\ge 0\) and \(R_{hkt}\ge 0\)
Resource consumption is additive across pattern executions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_p r_{hpk}x_{pkt}\le R_{hkt}\) for every \(h,k,t\).

notation.meaning: executions of pattern p on equipment k in period t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive capacity condition fits the leaf and content kind, but no cited source supports the cutting-equipment interpretation, and the index sets for patterns, resources, equipment, and periods are not explicitly introduced.

children.title: Cross-Chapter Operational Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Integrated models acknowledged without duplicating their primary operational theory.

children.title: Production-Inventory Temporal Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupling to production timing and inventory decisions.

children.title: Lot-Sizing Coupling
children.top_down_role: Links between cutting quantities and production-lot decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lot-Sizing Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard setup-linked lot-sizing interface for time-indexed cutting decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For stock type \(s\) and period \(t\), let \(q_{st}\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the produced lot and \(y_{st}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether production is set up. If cutting pattern \(p\) consumes \(b_{sp}\) units of stock type \(s\), the cutting and lot-sizing decisions are coupled by
\[q_{st}=\sum_p b_{sp}x_{pt},\qquad L_{st}y_{st}\le q_{st}\le U_{st}y_{st},\]
where \(0\le L_{st}\le U_{st}\). Thus positive pattern use requires an active lot, while the aggregate stock consumption equals the lot quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pattern executions determine each period’s lot quantity, which is permitted only when its setup is active and remains within lot bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{pt},q_{st}\in\mathbb Z_+\) and \(y_{st}\in\{0,1\}\)
\(b_{sp}\in\mathbb Z_+\)
\(0\le L_{st}\le U_{st}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{st}=\sum_p b_{sp}x_{pt}\) and \(L_{st}y_{st}\le q_{st}\le U_{st}y_{st}\).

notation.meaning: executions of cutting pattern p in period t
lot quantity of stock type s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible, but no source supports identifying aggregate stock consumption as the produced lot. The claim that any positive pattern use activates the setup also requires positive consumption by every usable pattern.

children.title: Inventory-Balance Coupling
children.top_down_role: Links between cutting plans and inventory states.

knowledge_statements.title: Inventory-Balance Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Material-flow balance connecting cutting output, demand, and inventory over time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For item \(i\) and period \(t\), let \(I_{it}\ge0\) denote end-of-period inventory, \(d_{it}\ge0\) demand, and \(a_{ip}\in\mathbb Z_+\) the yield of pattern \(p\). With pattern counts \(x_{pt}\in\mathbb Z_+\), exact demand fulfillment without backlogging is represented by
\[I_{i,t-1}+\sum_p a_{ip}x_{pt}=d_{it}+I_{it}\qquad\text{for every }i,t,\]
with initial inventory \(I_{i0}\) specified. The equality transfers surplus cutting output to later periods and forbids disposal unless a separate disposal variable is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prior inventory plus current cutting output equals current demand plus ending inventory for every item and period.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{pt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) and \(I_{it}\ge0\)
\(a_{ip}\in\mathbb Z_+\) and \(d_{it}\ge0\)
Backlogging and disposal are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_{i,t-1}+\sum_p a_{ip}x_{pt}=d_{it}+I_{it}\) for every \(i,t\).

notation.meaning: yield of item i from pattern p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inventory balance is mathematically standard and matches the leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for its cutting-stock specialization.

children.title: Multi-Period Cutting Decisions
children.top_down_role: Cutting-stock decisions distributed across multiple planning periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Period Cutting Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed cutting-stock formulation with inventory carryover and period capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{pt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) count executions of pattern \(p\) in period \(t\), and let \(I_{it}\ge0\) be ending inventory of item \(i\). Given yields \(a_{ip}\), demands \(d_{it}\), processing requirements \(r_{pt}\), capacities \(R_t\), and initial inventories \(I_{i0}\), multi-period cutting feasibility is represented by
\[I_{i,t-1}+\sum_p a_{ip}x_{pt}=d_{it}+I_{it}\quad(\forall i,t),\qquad \sum_p r_{pt}x_{pt}\le R_t\quad(\forall t).\]
An objective may add period-specific cutting, setup, holding, and shortage costs without changing this feasibility interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Period-indexed pattern counts jointly satisfy material balances and cutting capacity, allowing surplus output to be carried into later periods.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{pt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) and \(I_{it}\ge0\)
\(a_{ip},d_{it},r_{pt},R_t\ge0\)
\(I_{i0}\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed balance and capacity constraints hold for every applicable item and period.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The time-indexed representation fits the leaf, but no source is cited. The displayed exact-demand balance contains no shortage variable, so the statement that shortage costs may be added without changing the feasibility interface is unsupported and generally false.

children.title: Routing-Schedule Coordination Interface
children.top_down_role: Coupling to setup, due-date, and open-stack scheduling.

children.title: Pattern Sequencing Coupling
children.top_down_role: Links between pattern selection and execution order.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Sequencing Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition-based coupling between selected patterns and their execution order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n_p\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the required number of executions of pattern \(p\). Index the resulting execution slots by \(v\), let \(u_{vp}\in\{0,1\}\) assign a pattern to slot \(v\), and let \(z_{vw}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that slot \(w\) immediately follows slot \(v\). A feasible coupling satisfies
\[\sum_pu_{vp}=1,\qquad \sum_vu_{vp}=n_p,\]
and the selected arcs \(z_{vw}\) form one directed path through all slots. A transition cost or setup time from \(v\) to \(w\) is activated only when \(z_{vw}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pattern multiplicities determine assigned execution slots, while sequencing variables form one path and activate transition-dependent costs or setup times.
assumptions_latex: \(n_p\in\mathbb Z_+\)
Every required execution is represented by one slot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_pu_{vp}=1\), \(\sum_vu_{vp}=n_p\), and \(z\) defines one directed path through all slots.

notation.meaning: assignment of pattern p to execution slot v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The topic and condition role fit the leaf, but the degree, connectivity, and subtour-elimination constraints needed for one directed path are omitted, as is a precise link between slot arcs and pattern-dependent transitions. A source is needed to determine the intended complete formulation.

children.title: Production Scheduling Coupling
children.top_down_role: Links between cutting decisions and production schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Production Scheduling Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine scheduling constraints linked to individual cutting-pattern executions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be the set of selected cutting operations, with processing time \(p_v>0\), assigned machine \(m(v)\), start time \(S_v\ge0\), and completion time \(C_v=S_v+p_v\). For every distinct pair \(v,w\) on the same machine, a binary precedence variable \(z_{vw}\) enforces
\[S_w\ge C_v-M(1-z_{vw}),\qquad S_v\ge C_w-Mz_{vw},\]
for a valid upper-bound constant \(M\). Pattern-count decisions determine how many operations enter \(V\); the inequalities then prevent their processing intervals from overlapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected pattern executions become scheduled operations whose machine intervals cannot overlap and whose completion times follow their processing durations.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a valid scheduling-horizon bound.
Machines process at most one operation at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_v=S_v+p_v\) and operations assigned to the same machine have nonoverlapping intervals.

notation.meaning: start and completion times of operation v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scheduling interface is locally relevant, but the inequalities should be indexed once per unordered same-machine pair. Merely calling M a horizon bound does not state the variable bounds needed to make both disjunctions safely inactive, and no source resolves the formulation.

children.title: Due-Date Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Coordination of cutting plans with demand due dates.

knowledge_statements.title: Due-Date Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demand deadlines expressed through cumulative cutting output or tardiness variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For item \(i\), let \(d_i\) be its due date and \(D_i\) its required quantity. If pattern \(p\) started at time \(S_v\) completes at \(C_v\) and yields \(a_{ip}\) units when assigned to execution \(v\), on-time fulfillment requires
\[\sum_{v:C_v\le d_i}\sum_p a_{ip}u_{vp}\ge D_i.\]
Alternatively, if completion of order \(i\) is represented by \(C_i\), its tardiness interface is \(T_i\ge C_i-d_i\) and \(T_i\ge0\); imposing \(T_i=0\) recovers a hard due date.
